title: Receipts Over Genius: An Audited Account of an 18-Month, AI-Assisted, Solo Invention Cycle
abstract: SQUIRL OS RESEARCH DISCLOSURE - READ FIRST: This work is part of an open-book, AI-assisted research program produced under bifurcated governance (a probabilistic AI agent drafts; a deterministic human key approves; a boundary-layer audit checks claims against receipt archives). Audit-and-correction is doctrine: superseded originals are preserved in version histories, corrections are disclosed amendments, and every significant test carries a preregistered falsifier in the append-only public ledger (github.com/LLong2026/four-horsemen). This software and its accompanying research are prototypes provided for educational and research purposes only; they are not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. In April 2025 the author, a working technologist with no background in AI, set himself a falsifiable experiment: use AI assistance to travel the complete invention cycle - conceive, develop the mathematics, build the working system, file the patents, publish the science, demonstrate the result - with every significant step verified by a timestamped, publicly inspectable receipt. This paper is the closing account of that experiment, written under the same rules it describes. Result, scoped honestly: in 18 months a single operator completed the cycle - eight U.S. provisional patent applications pending; a working self-healing infrastructure platform across a live app fleet; the first documented caging of an LLM inside a deterministic mathematical boundary (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23265723), a receipt that survived direct third-party scrutiny; and a public research line (the DCAI community) walking from theory to governance proof to field event. Two findings carry the paper: (1) the experiment succeeded because of the boundary, not despite it - bifurcated governance turned the operator's lack of background into an auditable process; (2) the program generated its own counter-evidence, reported here rather than discarded: five cataloged instances of AI confabulation inside the program itself (fabricated statuses, fabricated evaluation data, a fabricated institutional identity), every one caught by the same receipt discipline the experiment was testing. The method worked on its author's own tooling. Thesis community: Deterministic Caged AI (DCAI) - https://zenodo.org/communities/dcai. Lineage acknowledged: Nyquist (1924), Hartley (1928), Shannon (1948), Kolmogorov (1965), Popper (1959). Companion paper: Deterministic Caging of Probabilistic Large Language Models (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23266727).

title: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) and Migration Strategies for Enterprise IT Infrastructure: Standards, Protocol Benchmarks, and Crypto-Agility
abstract: Abstract—The advent of fault-tolerant Cryptanalytically Relevant Quantum Computers (CRQCs) presents an existential threat to modern information security. Shor's polynomial-time quantum algorithm renders widely deployed public-key cryptographic primitives—including RSA, Diffie-Hellman (DH), and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECDH/ECDSA)—completely vulnerable to private key derivation. Furthermore, 'Harvest Now, Decrypt Later' (HNDL) adversarial campaigns actively intercept and store encrypted enterprise telemetry today, anticipating future quantum decryption capabilities. In response, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) finalized its primary Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) standards in FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA), and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA). However, transitioning complex enterprise IT ecosystems to quantum-resistant primitives introduces severe architectural and computational disruptions: public key and signature sizes increase by several orders of magnitude, cryptographic handshake latencies escalate, network packets experience Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) fragmentation, and legacy Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) lack microarchitectural support for lattice-based polynomial arithmetic. This paper provides an exhaustive, mathematically grounded technical survey and architectural roadmap for enterprise PQC migration. We formalize the Module Learning with Errors (M-LWE) and Module Short Integer Solution (M-SIS) hardness foundations, evaluate hybrid classical/post-quantum cryptographic transition models across standard transport protocols (TLS 1.3, IKEv2/IPsec, SSH), and formulate an enterprise Crypto-Agility Maturity Model. Furthermore, we construct an empirical enterprise testbed measuring throughput, connection establishment latency, memory footprints, and packet fragmentation across legacy and quantum-resistant suites. Our results show that while ML-KEM-768 achieves microsecond-level encapsulation, its 1,088-byte ciphertext expands TLS ClientHello payloads into multiple TCP segments under constrained networks. Finally, we establish open research directions in post-quantum identity federations, stateful hash signature tracking, and hardware-accelerated polynomial arithmetic. Index Terms—Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC), FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA), Crypto-Agility, TLS 1.3, Lattice-Based Cryptography, Harvest Now Decrypt Later, Hardware Security Modules (HSM), Enterprise Migration.

title: Edge AI and Federated Learning for Privacy-Preserving IoT Systems: System Architectures, Non-IID Optimization, and Security Bounds
abstract: Abstract—The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has created an unprecedented surge in decentralized telemetry, sensor data, and localized computational workloads. Conventional cloud-centric machine learning architectures require centralized pooling of raw edge data, which induces prohibitive wide-area network (WAN) bandwidth consumption, unsustainable latency, and acute privacy vulnerabilities under international compliance mandates (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA). The convergence of Edge AI and Federated Learning (FL) establishes an alternative computational paradigm where edge nodes perform local model optimization on private data, communicating solely parameterized weight or gradient updates to an aggregation coordinator. Nevertheless, deploying robust FL across heterogeneous IoT ecosystems introduces profound systems challenges: non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) data distributions, severe hardware resource disparities (memory, compute, power), communication bottlenecks over constrained wireless channels, and susceptibility to model inversion, gradient reconstruction, and Byzantine poisoning attacks. This paper delivers a comprehensive technical survey and systematic architectural formulation of privacy-preserving Edge-FL for IoT systems. We formalize the distributed optimization objective under statistical skew, analyze parameter-efficient edge acceleration techniques (including dynamic quantization and parameter-efficient fine-tuning), and evaluate cryptographic privacy mechanisms combining Differential Privacy (DP) and Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMPC). Furthermore, we conduct extensive empirical benchmarks across 100 heterogeneous edge nodes simulating industrial IoT, smart healthcare, and connected mobility workloads. Our results demonstrate that adaptive quantized federated aggregation achieves an 81.4% reduction in uplink communication bandwidth while preserving model accuracy within 1.6% of centralized benchmarks under severe statistical skew. Finally, we formulate open challenges in post-quantum cryptographic federated verification, asynchronous edge coordination, and green zero-carbon IoT optimization. Index Terms—Edge AI, Federated Learning, Internet of Things (IoT), Differential Privacy, Non-IID Optimization, Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning, Secure Multi-Party Computation, Edge Acceleration.

title: Agreement versus Softmax under Spatial Disambiguation
abstract: ScanRefer Multiple queries require spatial disambiguation: several instances of the target class are present, and the referencer must pick one. When per-query logits were never logged, a common substitute is cross-epoch agreement. On the full ScanRefer validation set (9,508 queries; GeoClassifier with ground-truth proposals), object-level softmax is similarly miscalibrated on Unique and Multiple (ECE 0.068 vs. 0.102; the scene-bootstrap gap interval includes zero). Fixed-final agreement on the same checkpoints reports ECE 0.041 vs. 0.272 (gap +0.231). Modal-vote agreement is 0.045 vs. 0.318. Most Multiple errors are same-class wrong-instance (45.6%); geometric miss (H2) is 59.6%, and wrong-category (H1) is 16.7%. A non-monotone H1 pattern does not appear under the default fixed-final protocol, and we retract it. Logit-free thresholds rank spatially hard queries poorly. If only agreement was logged, calibrate abstention on Multiple and report wrong-instance rates with H1.

title: Lifting an $[n,k,d]$ Binary Linear Code to an $[[n,k,d]]$ Quantum Stabilizer Code
abstract: The codeword stabilized (CWS) framework provides a systematic method for constructing quantum error correcting codes from a simple undirected graph and a classical code. When the underlying classical code is linear, the resulting quantum code is a stabilizer code. In this work, we investigate the conditions under which an arbitrary $[n,k,d]$ classical binary linear code can be lifted to an $[[n,k,d]]$ quantum stabilizer code using the CWS framework. We analyze the random CWS code constructed from a given $[n,k,d]$ binary linear code $\mathcal{C}$ and an Erdős-Rényi random graph $\mathrm{G}(n, \frac12)$. We establish a lower bound on the probability that the resulting quantum code preserves the minimum distance $d$ of the classical code. This probabilistic analysis yields a Gilbert-Varshamov-type condition on the $n,k,d$ parameters of the classical code that guarantees the existence of a graph resulting in a quantum code with the same $n,k,d$ parameters.

title: Deep Learning Approach for RealTime Contraction Detection in Laboring Dairy Cattle
abstract: Currently, the animal production sector is undergoing rapid development of techniques that allow automatic monitoring of animal behaviour and health. This paper presents a computer vision-based approach for the automatic recognition of labor contractions in cows. During the course of the study, videos depicting 100 cow births were collected. From the obtained videos, 8500 cow contraction actions and about 25 000 non-contraction sequences were extracted which constituted the dataset. Leveraging image processing techniques and deep learning algorithms like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs), our methodology extracts relevant features from video frames to detect and classify contractions. Our study demonstrates a high accuracy rate of over 95% in detecting labor contractions. This automated system has the potential to enhance productivity and animal welfare in the dairy industry by providing real-time monitoring and facilitating timely intervention during difficult calvings. The video demonstration of the system can be found at the following URL: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8fTSG5D7dZ0

title: QCLR: A Plug-in Robustification Module via Quantization for Contrastive Learning in Self-Supervised Skeleton-Based Human Action Recognition
abstract: Skeleton-based human action recognition has gained increasing attention due to the stability of skeleton data across diverse environments and advances in motion capture technologies. Following the success of supervised learning approaches, self-supervised learning approaches, particularly contrastive learning ones, have achieved impressive performance. However, they remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks. In this work, we propose a plug-in robustification module via quantization for contrastive learning in self-supervised skeleton-based human action recognition (QCLR), which enhances the robustness of representations against adversarial attacks while preserving their representational capability. Specifically, we employ a dual-level quantization scheme across the encoding pipeline, which breaks the gradient propagation and absorbs small adversarial perturbations within the quantization bins. To mitigate the impact of inevitable quantization error, we further design an attention-guided multi-faceted quantization strategy to maintain the representation quality. Experiments on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that integrating QCLR into a progressive lineage of mainstream contrastive learning models substantially improves robustness against both gradient-based white-box and gradient-free black-box adversarial attacks, while preserving highly competitive classification accuracy.

title: Constructing Pareto Frontiers of Optimal Reasoning Termination Methods for Overthinking in Reasoning Models
abstract: Reasoning models can benefit from test-time scaling, but continued reasoning may become ineffective or harmful, a phenomenon termed overthinking. Evaluations against full thinking compare accuracy and token usage but lack references for overthinking severity and strategies' theoretical mitigation potential. To characterize overthinking at the model-task level, we first introduce Step-wise Truncation Probing (STP), repeatedly generating answers from multiple retained prefixes along each fixed sampled reasoning trajectory. Using each trajectory's earliest measured position attaining maximum empirical accuracy as a reference, we define Overthinking Ratio and Accuracy Degradation as the fraction of thinking tokens generated afterward and the accuracy decrease from this reference to full thinking, respectively. Secondly, we then formulate dynamic routing, fixed budgets, and dynamic early exit within a unified framework to quantify the theoretical mitigation potential of different termination strategies. Based on this unified framework, we use the complete STP measurements to construct a token-accuracy Pareto frontier for each strategy under a common normalized thinking-token budget. We further develop OTBench, a reusable benchmark built from the STP process, which produced 70.5B reasoning tokens and the corresponding probing measurements across six models and four benchmark groups.

title: Human and LLM Facilitation in Collaborative Design Meetings: A Computational Behavioral Comparison
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored as facilitators of group discussion and collaborative work, but the behavioral differences between LLM-generated and human facilitation remain insufficiently characterized. We compare human Project Manager facilitation turns from scenario-based collaborative design meetings with Llama 3.1 8B Instruct responses across 199 paired contexts from the AMI Meeting Corpus. The analysis covers five confirmatory dimensions: contextual semantic distance, a lexical elaboration proxy, empathyand-hedge lexical density, topic divergence, and phase-vocabulary alignment. An exploratory directiveness measure failed domain validation and is not interpreted. The sampled human Project Manager turns were higher on contextual semantic distance (r = 0.644) and on empathyand-hedge lexical density (r = 0.203). The second contrast is carried mainly by hedge terms, so we read it as lexical hedging rather than psychological empathy. Llama-generated facilitation was higher on topic divergence (r = 0.703), the lexical elaboration proxy (r = 0.288; lengthconfounded), and instruction-conditioned phase-vocabulary alignment (r = 0.382). A secondary no-phase check left the Llama-higher phase contrast in place. The system prompt still requested a facilitation move, so that check is not evidence of spontaneous phase awareness. These differences should not be interpreted as a ranking of facilitation quality. The resulting behavioral profile provides a reference point for later comparisons of LLM facilitators, human facilitators, prompts, models, and collaborative settings.

title: Heteroskedastic Gaussian processes for ecological forecasting
abstract: Modern stochastic simulators and ecological time series share a common challenge: they exhibit input dependent noise. In such situations, accurate predictions into the future along with principled uncertainty are essential. Heteroskedastic Gaussian processes (hetGPs) are a flexible and nonparametric modeling technique wherein, two processes are inferred simul- taneously – the mean response and the latent noise levels corresponding to input locations. title: Theory of Everything Research Programme: Block IV Adaptive Agency and Structural Generalisation Confirmatory Dataset and Decision Record.
abstract: This dataset release provides the original confirmatory evidence and preregistered decision record for Experimental Block IV of the Theory of Everything Research Programme. The study was preregistered at OSF under DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/REHW5 before any held-out confirmatory seed was executed. The release contains seven provenance-valid confirmatory raw study trees generated from twenty held-out seeds, including trajectory records, causal-reversal adaptation measures, planning-horizon records, model-free bypass comparisons, world-model corruption and correction interventions, structural-novelty profiles, heuristic controls, seed registries, provenance metadata, processed metrics and decision records. The preregistered decisions were RETAIN for H4.1 through H4.7. A3 adapted to the held-out causal reversal in a median of one interaction versus ten for A4PLUS. Counterfactual-rollout success switched exactly when the rollout horizon reached each preregistered decisive consequence depth, and A3 exceeded A2 on held-out composition and problem-family tasks. The compute/storage-matched A4PLUS control matched A3 on interpolation, parameter variation and the delayed-family control but fell to 0.15 and 0.10 on composition and problem-family novelty while A3 remained at 1.00. Targeted corruption of task-relevant world-model content reduced A3 success from 1.00 to 0.00 in both registered structural families, whereas irrelevant corruption left success at 1.00; restoring the nominated model relation rescued performance to 1.00. A3 achieved 1.00 across all registered structural families, while no single preregistered simple heuristic reproduced that complete profile. All seven confirmatory runs completed once with provenance PASS and exactly twenty registered seeds per study. Independent analysis regeneration reproduced both substantive analysis artefacts byte-for-byte. This release is paired with the Block IV software and reproducibility package (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23263492) and implements the experimental framework described in Working Paper III (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22857230). The results support model-based control and counterfactual rollout as causally useful within the registered task families but do not establish universal necessity of world models, general intelligence, reflective self-awareness or phenomenal consciousness.

title: Theory of Everything Research Programme: Block IV Adaptive Agency and Structural Generalisation Confirmatory Experiment Software and Reproducibility Package.
abstract: This software release provides the executable and reproducibility infrastructure for the preregistered confirmatory study in Experimental Block IV of the Theory of Everything Research Programme. The package implements the frozen protocol associated with OSF preregistration DOI 10.17605/OSF.IO/REHW5. It contains seven frozen confirmatory manifests and integrity locks, twenty held-out seeds, confirmatory-only causal-reversal, delayed-consequence, compositional and problem-family variants, explicit implementations of reactive, history-sensitive model-free, predictive-model-only, counterfactual-rollout and capacity-matched model-free architectures, preregistered heuristic bypasses, world-model corruption and correction interventions, rollout-horizon ablations, provenance capture, automated decision logic and reproducibility tests. The confirmatory study returned RETAIN for H4.1 through H4.7. A3 adapted to the held-out causal reversal in a median of one interaction versus ten for A4PLUS; rollout success switched at the preregistered decisive consequence depth; A3 exceeded the compute/storage-matched A4PLUS control on held-out composition and problem-family novelty while matching it on interpolation, parameter variation and the delayed-family control; targeted world-model corruption reduced success from 1.00 to 0.00 in both registered structural families while irrelevant corruption left performance at 1.00 and correction restored it to 1.00; and no single preregistered heuristic reproduced A3's complete cross-family structural-generalisation profile. These results support explicit model-based control and counterfactual rollout as causally useful routes to structural generalisation within the registered artificial task families. They do not establish that world models are universally necessary, that model-free systems cannot generalise structurally under other architectures, or that structural generalisation is equivalent to general intelligence, reflective self-awareness or phenomenal consciousness. This release is paired with the Block IV confirmatory dataset and decision record (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23263512) and implements the experimental methodology described in Working Paper III (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22857230).

title: An Overview of Knowledge-Based System: History, Advances and Challenges in the Era of Large Language Models
abstract: With 60 years of research, knowledge-based system has travelled a long journey from early small-scale rule-based programs to modern super-large-scale knowledge graphs. Several multithreading technical stages can be broadly categorized: early history of rule-based system, knowledge engineering, semantic network, semantic web, ontology engineering, knowledge graph, and recent advances driven by machine learning. In the past couple years, the whole area of artificial intelligence including knowledge-based system has been significantly influenced by large language models, which dramatically increases the understanding and utilization of knowledge by increasing to an extremely large scale. Considering the long-standing intrinsic problems of large language models such as hallucination and lack of explainability, the challenge of how to build reliable large-scale knowledge-based systems in an effective and economical way still exists. From the overview of the developing history, we can see a promising research direction of combining large language models with those traditional knowledge-based frameworks.

title: Analysis of Sentiment in Tamil Comments Using BERT and Explainable AI
abstract: Due to the popularity of social media, an increasing number of people are expressing opinions and information in online spaces in many languages, especially Tamil and what is known as code-mixed Tamil-English. The analysis of these sentiments is important to businesses, media, and researchers trying to understand the larger constructs of public opinion. In this regard, Tamil presents a unique challenge for sentiment analysis, in part, due to its richer morphology than English, informal and slang use, and frequent code-mixing with English. The framework presented in this paper was created with Tamil and Tamil-English code-mixed text sentiment analysis. It relies on transformer-based language models, i.e., robust models like bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERT), IndicBERT and XLM-R that were additionally fine-tuned on Tamil data. Finally, we further improve model performance with character-level features extracted via CNN. This hybrid representation allows the model to have a greater ability to capture variations in spelling, slang, and informal language. Explainability is a key component of our system, along with performance. The LIME (Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations) method is used to provide interpretability to the framework by highlighting which words contributed most to the model's decision when classifying a text as positive, negative, or neutral. Our results show that the combination of lexicon features added to the BERT model improves the performance of the sentiment classification task. Furthermore, the BERT model has been compared against models like IndicBERT and XLM-R, with and without enabling lexicon support, based on performance metrics, run-time efficiency and memory use. The present work shows a useful and explainable analysis of sentiment for Tamil, a language that is typically marginalized in terms of its presence in the natural language processing space while also providing a potential path forward in directing future research of other low-resource and code-mixed languages.

title: Should SLMs be in the Driver's Seat? A Study of Local Models as Interpreters in Cloud-Written Agent Programs
abstract: The most accurate agents executing user-provided tasks are driven by large, cloud-hosted models, which solve them by reading the private data of the user. Agents powered by models small enough to run on edge devices keep that data local, but yield far worse results. A third option is to have cloud models write a program that devices execute: the data stays local, but as the program is written before any data is seen, it fails whenever a step depends on interpreting content that appears only at run time. We explore an intermediate architecture, in which the cloud-written program defers bounded questions over user data to a small local model through an ordinary function call. On AppWorld this improves the success rate of a code-only agent in all six combinations of backbone model and test partition we evaluate, by up to 14.9pp, recovering a substantial part of the gap to a cloud-hosted ReAct loop while keeping user data on the device.

title: CopRoute: Dependence-Aware Conformal Routing for Language Models
abstract: Set-based language model routing aims to increase the coverage of the event where at least one model answers a query correctly while controlling the number of inference calls made. Existing risk-controlled routing policies bound the all-miss risk (the probability that every model in the selected set fails) by calibrating a single conformal threshold and applying it to a nested family of model sets. Because each model is scored in isolation, these policies ignore the dependence structure of model failures. Models that share training data or architecture tend to fail on the same queries, so two individually strong models can be jointly redundant while a weaker but complementary model covers the queries that the others miss. To account for this dependence, which existing risk-controlled policies ignore, we propose CopRoute, which orders models by how many new queries each one answers correctly beyond those already selected, decides per query how far down that order to go, and then picks the smallest cutoff that still meets the target risk. We show that CopRoute's ordering attains, on the design data, the best guarantee any efficient fixed-ordering algorithm can give for the average number of calls to the first correct model, and that a separate calibration step certifies the all-miss risk of the deployed sets. On RouterBench and RouterEval, CopRoute attains the fewest certified calls on nine of ten datasets at a target risk of 0.05 and on eight of ten at 0.10, making up to 79 percent fewer calls (median 24 percent) than the state-of-the-art risk-controlled policy at the same certified all-miss risk.

title: Sistem Pemilihan Jurusan Kuliah Bagi Siswa SMK Berdasarkan Minat, Bakat dan Tes Akademik Menggunakan Algoritma K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN) Berbasis Web (Studi Kasus: SMK Avicena Rajeg)
abstract: Pemilihan jurusan perguruan tinggi sering kali menjadi kendala bagi siswa Sekolah Menengah Kejuruan (SMK) karena keterbatasan informasi dan kecenderungan memilih tanpa pertimbangan yang matang. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk membangun sistem pendukung keputusan berbasis web menggunakan algoritma K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN) guna membantu siswa SMK Avicena Rajeg dalam menentukan jurusan kuliah yang sesuai dengan minat, bakat, dan nilai akademik. Sistem ini bekerja dengan menghitung jarak antara data siswa dan data latih menggunakan metode Euclidean Distance, kemudian menentukan rekomendasi berdasarkan tiga tetangga terdekat (K = 3). Hasil dari penelitian ini berupa aplikasi web yang dapat memberikan rekomendasi jurusan secara objektif sehingga membantu siswa mengambil keputusan studi lanjut dengan lebih tepat. Proses pengembangan sistem pendukung keputusan ini diawali dengan pengumpulan data kriteria yang mencakup nilai rapot akademik, hasil tes minat bakat, serta pilihan kecenderungan pribadi siswa. Data tersebut kemudian diolah dan dinormalisasi agar perhitungan jarak antar variabel pada algoritma KNN dapat berjalan secara akurat. Selanjutnya, sistem diuji menggunakan metode confusion matrix untuk mengukur tingkat akurasi, presisi, dan sensitivitas rekomendasi yang dihasilkan. Melalui keberadaan sistem pendukung keputusan berbasis web ini, diharapkan dapat meminimalkan risiko kesalahan dalam pemilihan jurusan di tingkat perguruan tinggi yang sering dialami oleh lulusan sekolah kejuruan. Selain memberikan kemudahan akses bagi para siswa, sistem ini juga berfungsi sebagai alat bantu navigasi bagi guru bimbingan konseling (BK) di SMK Avicena Rajeg dalam memberikan arahan studi lanjut yang lebih terarah, terukur, dan berbasis data ilmiah.

title: Explainable automated classification of cervical cancer cells using SE-LGANet with squeeze and excitation blocks and local and global attention mechanisms
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a significant global health threat, making early detection through Pap Smear screenings essential for improving survival rates. This study aims to enhance the classification of cervical cell categories using the SIPaKMeD dataset, focusing on increasing diagnostic accuracy and model interpretability. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) integrated with Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) blocks and dual attention mechanisms was developed to classify five distinct cell types: Koilocytotic, Parabasal, Superficial-Intermediate, Dyskeratotic, and Metaplastic cells. Grad-CAM was utilized to visualize lesion areas and ensure model interpretability. The architecture was further validated using Mendeley LBC and Herlev datasets. The proposed model achieved 91.48% accuracy, 91.57% sensitivity, and 97.87% specificity on the SIPaKMeD dataset. It also demonstrated high transferability with 96.88% accuracy on Mendeley LBC and 89.62% on the Herlev dataset. Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP confirmed the model’s focus on clinically relevant features. The integration of attention mechanisms and interpretability tools provides an explainable and systematically validated approach for cervical cell evaluation. This framework bridges the gap between AI performance and clinical trust, with future research focusing on real-world clinical integration.

The integration of attention mechanisms and interpretability tools provides an explainable and systematically validated approach for cervical cell evaluation. This framework bridges the gap between AI performance and clinical trust, with future research focusing on real-world clinical integration.

title: Token-Budgeted Candidate Retrieval for 3D Scene-Grounded VLMs: Category Names vs. Pairwise Geometry
abstract: Under a fixed context budget, which objects and relations should a 3D scene-grounded VLM see first? On ScanNet indoor referring benchmarks (Dai et al., 2017), matching the query to object category names outperforms pairwise geometry scoring at every reported K. The gaps are largest at high recall. Analytic pairwise cues beat per-object cue scoring and query-agnostic kNN graphs, including on paraphrases. MiniLM and BGE-small still score higher on those splits. We evaluate token-budgeted candidate retrieval with axis-aligned boxes, a token-ratio metric, training-free baselines, two small encoders that match q to each object's category name, and QCRR (Query-Conditioned Relation Retrieval), a deterministic pairwise-geometry scorer. Across ScanRefer gt_val plus a custom 20% scan-id split of Nr3D and Sr3D (35,504 queries; not official ReferIt3D val), additive noun matching reaches R@10 0.864 on ScanRefer against QCRR's 0.626; MiniLM and BGE-small reach 0.911 to 0.913 on ScanRefer and 0.941 to 0.947 on Nr3D. A corrected 3DGraphLLM harness (native Acc@0.25 0.67 on the full graph, n=300 ScanRefer queries) shows that context selection changes downstream accuracy under a matched object budget (Random 0.44, QCRR 0.56, MiniLM 0.67, oracle 0.70). Semantic retrieval beats hand-designed geometry on that harness. We will release the protocol, retriever implementations, and per-query outputs so new selectors can be swapped in without rewriting the analysis.

title: KVeil: First-Place Solution to ECCV 2026 LifeGenIP Challenge on Unlearnable Videos
abstract: The rapid development of personalized video generation has raised serious concerns over identity privacy, as a few facial videos of a person now suffice to reproduce their identity in synthetic videos. This report presents the first-place solutions to both phases of the ECCV 2026 LifeGenIP Challenge on Unlearnable Videos, which aims to protect facial videos from unauthorized customization under a limited and imperceptible perturbation budget. For Phase 1, we introduce Reference Capacity Collapse, a pair of complementary losses that degrade the information carried by the reference condition while keeping subsequent video representations dependent on it, together with a Motion-Guided EOT mechanism that improves robustness across unknown inference conditions. Phase 2 further considers tuning-based customization and unseen generative models. To address both threats within a single perturbation, we design a two-layer framework that protects the facial and background regions separately, constructing structure-aligned perturbations from a synthetic target identity in the former and strengthening the white-box disruption of Phase 1 in the latter. Our method achieves nearly perfect protection under white-box reference-based customization, and remains effective under other customization paradigms, various models, and temporal attacks. Both solutions are built upon our recent work LETHE. We hope our solutions can inspire future work on protecting facial videos against unauthorized customization. Our code is available at https://github.com/AntigoneRandy/KVeil.

title: A Scalable Learned Iterative Solver for Nonlinear MPC via Temporal Decomposition
abstract: Nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) can be applied to large nonlinear systems with complex objectives while enforcing constraints, but the cost of solving the underlying optimization problems limits real-time application for systems with fast dynamics or many states. Neural networks can reduce this online cost by approximating the control law, but may violate constraints and typically require many precomputed optimizer solutions for training. The learning-based iterative solver for constrained optimization (LISCO) instead learns to predict primal-dual steps toward satisfaction of the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions through self-supervised training without precomputed solutions, but its dense, monolithic architecture grows with the prediction horizon. We remove this horizon dependence by exploiting the temporal structure of the problem in the solver architecture, which makes the network size independent of the horizon while leaving the training loss and the solver iteration unchanged. A closed-loop resampling strategy further aligns the training distribution with closed-loop operation at no additional sampling cost. On an economic NMPC benchmark of a CSTR cascade, the proposed solver scales to larger problems than monolithic LISCO and achieves median speedups of up to a factor of four over IPOPT. In closed loop, it achieves comparable control performance to IPOPT with no observed constraint violations.

title: REFLECT: Role-Aware Detection of Sentiment, Emotion, Politeness, and Formality
abstract: Detecting communicative meaning in dialogue requires modeling not only lexical content but also the participant-role structures through which sentiment, emotion, politeness, and formality (SEPF) are expressed. Existing approaches rely on contextual language representations while leaving semantic roles implicit. We introduce a role-aware transformer architecture that maps the four SEPF dimensions to theory-grounded Semantic Role Labeling (SRL) configurations, incorporating these configurations directly into the transformer's self-attention mechanism. Role-aware attention models non-directional internal states (sentiment and emotion), while directional role-aware attention captures initiator-to-recipient relations for external cues (politeness and formality). The resulting role-aware representations are fused with contextual embeddings through a learned gate that adaptively weights how much role information each input contributes, rather than appending semantic roles as an auxiliary feature vector. Across four benchmark datasets, the framework yields statistically reliable gains over strong BERT-based baselines for emotion, politeness, and formality, with gains concentrated in theoretically predicted cases such as low-frequency, complex emotions and highly polite expressions; sentiment improvements are marginal and non-significant, suggesting that sentiment is conveyed more through lexical choice than participant-role structure. Additional evaluation on real-world data demonstrates that the framework improves both predictive performance and model traceability. These results demonstrate that linguistically grounded modifications to transformer self-attention improve the detection of communicative meaning, generalize beyond benchmark datasets to real-world mental-health data, and yield traceable, role-grounded explanations that extend beyond predictive performance to interpretability.

title: Target-Constrained Pooling for Trajectory Extrapolation
abstract: Trajectory extrapolation from a partial target trajectory is underdetermined, but completed related trajectories provide information about the unresolved continuation. We propose target-constrained pooling (TCP), which separates the finite-horizon endpoint from continuation shape and estimates that endpoint from two complementary source signals. Uniform pooling captures final response levels, while matched-increment pooling captures the remaining change after aligning source and target states. TCP selects representative sources, projects both endpoint estimates onto a target-consistent region, converts them into corrections of the free forecast, and controls their influence through strength calibration and degradation-aware weighting. Across 25,245 targets from five domains and both forecasting directions, TCP reduces mean RMSE by 35.8% to 42.1% for all ten target-only forecasters and improves all 100 forecaster, dataset, and direction comparisons. The two endpoint signals consistently outperform either alone, while representative selection remains within 0.64% to 1.02% of the full donor pool using 12.7x fewer donor inputs and 138.8x fewer matching distance computations.

title: From Tongue to Mind: From Prompt Engineering to Mind Engineering
abstract: Large language models speak remarkably well, but they were not built to judge: their opinions shift between conversations, they invent numbers with confidence, and they lean toward whoever is asking. Agents then gave these models hands to act on what they had guessed. This whitepaper tells how that problem led to a different idea: to put a deterministic mind — one that thinks and decides under written law — in the seat of judgment, in place of the language model, which stays a tongue that understands the user and puts the reply into words. The paper calls this category Mind Intelligence, and the language model's share Language Intelligence. Its units are artificial minds; engineered personas wear them; and a composite mind brings them together. The discipline of building them is Mind Engineering, set against prompt engineering: prompt engineering shapes the tongue; mind engineering builds the judge. A prompt that tells a model "you are a CFO" changes its style, not its judgment — a finding supported by recent research; mind engineering builds the CFO instead. The paper follows the idea from its origin — repeated conversations in which the same messages produced different opinions, a study of prompt engineering that showed prompts shape the tongue but not the mind, the Seventh Mind and the first version of GAIBRA — to its embodiment in a platform of more than thirty personas, each with its own mind, law and deterministic thinking engines. It sets out the philosophy (never silent, never pretending, never flattering, never lying; consistency before eloquence; appearance does not change substance; law before code), the seven-layer anatomy of an artificial mind, the path of a request, personas in place of prompts, councils, memory, how claims are checked, and what the architecture does not yet guarantee. The framework — artificial minds, engineered personas in place of prompts, Mind Engineering as the discipline of building them, the composite mind, and Mind Intelligence as a layer of judgment between language models and agents — was introduced by Abdullah Eliyan, Co-founder & CEO of ANSANA and architect of GAIBRA, in 2026. GAIBRA runs on servers in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Two language editions are included: English and Arabic.

title: Two-photon induced coherence without induced emission
abstract: At the heart of recent breakthroughs in quantum imaging and spectroscopy using undetected photons lies the quantum-optical effect known as induced coherence without induced emission. This fundamental quantum interference effect has unlocked new possibilities in accessing challenging wavelength regimes for advanced imaging and spectroscopic analysis. Despite these advancements, the full spectrum of quantum metrology's capabilities, particularly the enhanced phase sensitivity offered by quantum optical Fock states or N00N states, has yet to be realized. This is because, until now, the exploration of induced coherence has been confined to phenomena involving single photons. In this study, we present the observation of two-photon-induced coherence without induced emission. This advancement hinges on a two-photon Fock state that establishes quantum coherence between pairs of two-photon spontaneous-emission amplitudes. The result is a doubling of the interferometric phase modulation compared to what is observed with single photons. Specifically, we show that a phase change 𝝓 applied to undetected 1016 nm near-infrared photons leads to 2𝝓 modulation in the detection.

title: Deeplay: enhancing PyTorch with customizable and reusable neural networks
abstract: Deeplay is a Python-based deep learning library that extends PyTorch, addressing limitations in modularity and reusability commonly encountered in neural network development. Built with a core philosophy of modularity and adaptability. Unlike traditional PyTorch modules, Deeplay allows the properties of submodules to be modified after creation. Layers, blocks, or activation functions can be replaced or reconfigured without rewriting the surrounding architecture, which reduces boilerplate code, improves reuse, and simplifies ablation studies.

title: Refined Grid Sampling for Efficient Implicit Neural Representations of Large-Scale Scientific Data
abstract: Implicit neural representations (INRs) offer a powerful framework for modeling high-dimensional physical fields, but their training remains inefficient because evaluating dense coordinate grids is computationally expensive. Existing coordinate-pruning strategies rely on local error functions that can oversample correlated points and incur substantial overhead from full-grid error evaluation. We introduce Refined Grid Sampling (RGS), which combines stratified grid sampling, error-based refinement, and dynamic grid-resolution adjustment. This design reduces spatial redundancy without evaluating errors over the full grid. On high-resolution Navier--Stokes fields, RGS achieves higher reconstruction accuracy within a fixed wall-clock budget and reaches the accuracy of full-grid training up to $6\times$ faster than the evaluated baselines.

title: LAPT-Scale: Scaling Embodied Policies with Latent Action Pre-Training on Human Videos
abstract: Scaling generalist robotic policies is limited by the high cost of collecting embodied interaction data. Large-scale egocentric human videos offer a rich alternative, but they lack robot action labels, and existing action annotation methods are often noisy under real-world visual complexity and diverse manipulation dynamics. We introduce LAPT-Scale, a scalable latent action pre-training paradigm with two components: LAPT-Scale-LAM learns continuous latent actions by explaining frame-to-frame visual transitions in human videos and uses them as human-derived supervision, while LAPT-Scale-Policy trains a VLA policy through human-video latent-action pre-training, target-robot embodiment alignment, and task-specific post-training. Unlike prior vector-quantized LAMs, LAPT-Scale-LAM uses a continuous latent space to preserve fine-grained motion and interaction dynamics. We further combine perceptual, semantic, and optical-flow alignment signals to improve transition-level supervision beyond pixel reconstruction. Trained on 23.3K hours of egocentric video, LAPT-Scale-LAM provides implicit action supervision for policy pre-training, yielding consistent scaling gains and improving real-robot success from 63.3% to 85.0% as annotated human video scales from 1K to 5K hours. The learned policy also generalizes to unseen visual conditions.

title: A Local Agentic AI Framework to Generate Edge Case Scenarios for Safety Assurance
abstract: Generating edge case scenarios is crucial for training, testing and safety assuring autonomous systems. This identifies hazardous failures to increase system reliability and robustness, ensures the system can still function safely on the boundaries of its operational design domain and learns the expected system behaviour for these edge cases. The rapid advancement in the generation and analysis capabilities of language models (LMs) has expanded their applicability and recent work has investigated LM scenario generation. However, many recent approaches rely on human-in-the-loop or rule-based strategies. This restricts the LM's ability to generate diverse and edge case scenarios; the long tail of the distribution. Our work uses local LMs in a laptop-based agentic AI framework for adaptive scenario generation. This is cheap, fully-controlled, ensures data privacy and security. It uses think, act, observe, update, and continue loops with lightweight JSON encoding to generate scenarios. We use the system requirements, system description and environment description as knowledge bases in contextual prompts for an LM to ensure scenario realism. A second, independent LM critiques each scenario using domain specific criteria so it can be refined. The refined scenarios are run in simulation and evaluation metrics collected. These metric scores are analysed and similar scenarios are created for edge cases (exploitation) or novel scenarios are generated to explore the scenario space. Post-hoc clustering using metric scores and thematic-type analysis of the rich-text scenario descriptions produced by the LM pinpoints functional gaps and their triggering conditions. This creates traceable evidence for the safety assurance case. evidence.title: A Local Agentic AI Framework to Generate Edge Case Scenarios for Safety Assurance
evidence.abstract: Generating edge case scenarios is crucial for training, testing and safety assuring autonomous systems. This identifies hazardous failures to increase system reliability and robustness, ensures the system can still function safely on the boundaries of its operational design domain and learns the expected system behaviour for these edge cases. The rapid advancement in the generation and analysis capabilities of language models (LMs) has expanded their applicability and recent work has investigated LM scenario generation. However, many recent approaches rely on human-in-the-loop or rule-based strategies. This restricts the LM's ability to generate diverse and edge case scenarios; the long tail of the distribution. Our work uses local LMs in a laptop-based agentic AI framework for adaptive scenario generation. This is cheap, fully-controlled, ensures data privacy and security. It uses think, act, observe, update, and continue loops with lightweight JSON encoding to generate scenarios. We use the system requirements, system description and environment description as knowledge bases in contextual prompts for an LM to ensure scenario realism. A second, independent LM critiques each scenario using domain specific criteria so it can be refined. The refined scenarios are run in simulation and evaluation metrics collected. These metric scores are analysed and similar scenarios are created for edge cases (exploitation) or novel scenarios are generated to explore the scenario space. Post-hoc clustering using metric scores and thematic-type analysis of the rich-text scenario descriptions produced by the LM pinpoints functional gaps and their triggering conditions. This creates traceable evidence for the safety assurance case. Our work highlights the potential of a flexible and adaptive local agentic AI framework for automating edge case generation and producing traceable safety assurance evidence.

title: The Predictability Bias of Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning in Medical Imaging
abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn by predicting teacher representations of masked regions from visible context. Point prediction summarizes the conditional target distribution and cannot reproduce variation that the context does not resolve. We call this constraint predictability bias. In computed tomography (CT), recurrent anatomy is predictable from context, whereas the sporadic, localized pathology that determines clinical interpretation often is not. We introduce TAP-JEPA, a ViT-B/3D trained on 113,611 CT volumes that is competitive with state-of-the-art encoders (COLIPRI, Merlin, VoxelFM) in scan-level classification. We then audit the learned predictive pathway by replaying the exact masking, teacher, and predictor computations used during training. Prediction lowers the mean Skill (prevalence-normalized average precision) from 0.388 to 0.271 for pathology, but only from 0.921 to 0.873 for anatomy. Along the teacher direction, separating pathology from matched control regions in the same organ, prediction moves pathology 34.7% toward the controls and controls 13.6% toward pathology, with larger shifts farther from visible context. Replacing visible matched-control representations increases surrounding-target prediction loss more than fully replacing pathology representations across four pathology categories. Downstream, removing all final-layer pathology tokens reduces the decision margin by at most 0.45% in four of seven scan-level probes. Together, these results show that contextual predictability is not a sufficient proxy for clinical relevance in medical representation learning. Training objectives should therefore retain diagnostic features regardless of their predictability from surrounding anatomy.

title: Automatic Lymphocyte Detection On Gastric Cancer Using Deep Learning
abstract: Gastric cancer still has rather high rates of incidences around the globe and the amount of tumor infiltrating lymphocytes in the tumor tissues has proved to be a reliable predictor of prognosis in patients suffering from this type of disease. At this point, the manual count of TILs had been performed by pathologists on tissue samples stained and analyzed under microscope. The paper suggests a fully automated pipeline for detecting lymphocytes in the histological pictures of patients with gastric cancer using YOLOv5 detector with ResNet-50 backbone. Namely, the pipeline presupposes slicing the picture into overlapped tiles, colour stain distribution normalization based on the Macenko algorithm, data set augmentation, and providing the slices to detection head that was upgraded by means of feature pyramid network, anchor optimization by k-means and convolutional block attention module, allowing for highlighting the features specific for lymphocytes. Duplications in the tile borders are handled through non-maximum suppression and weighted box fusion. As the data set used for testing is quite small, the precision of detections exceeded 92% and exact values of precision, recall and F1-score should be determined once the training is over. Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) are important indicators in cancer research because their abundance and distribution can be associated with prognosis and other clinical characteristics. For pathologists, identifying these immune cells in gastric cancer tissue images.

title: NEXUS: An MCP-Based Personal Productivity Agent with Dual-LLM Failover and Human-in-the-Loop Safety
abstract: Large Language Model agents have made it possibleto talk with digital tools using everyday language but creatingsystems that are dependable and safe requires good organizationof models, integration of tools in parts and careful control ofhow the system runs. This paper introduces NEXUS, a personalproductivity agent that uses the Model Context Protocol (MCP)to carry out tasks that need steps through natural-languageconversation. NEXUS uses Google Gemini as its LLM anduses Groq-hosted Llama 3.3 70B as a backup model givinga second way to think when the main model fails. NEXUSfollows a Think–Act–Observe routine: first NEXUS reads theuser’s request then NEXUS decides what action is needed thenNEXUS asks the tool via MCP then NEXUS checks the outcomeand finally NEXUS writes the response. NEXUS works withFilesystem, To-Do and Web Search MCP services. The customTo-Do service stores task data in SQLite lets users manage taskskeeps a log of changes and allows undo actions. NEXUS also hasa Human-in-the-Loop feature that asks the user to confirm beforeany change that alters the system state is carried out. NEXUScan also start tasks on its own. Can communicate with outsidesystems through its built-in services. By keeping the thinking partof the LLM separate, from the tool actions and by using modelbackup and strict tool controls NEXUS offers a system that’smodular, dependable and able to grow for personal productivity.

title: Napredki in perspektive v raziskavah govorne komunikacije
abstract: Okrogla miza z naslovom Napredki in perspektive v raziskavah govor­ne komunikacije je potekala na konferenci Jezikovne tehnologije in digitalna humanistika (JTDH) 19. 9. 2024 na Fakulteti za elektroteh­niko Univerze v Ljubljani. Izvedena je bila v okviru aktivnosti projekta Temeljne raziskave za razvoj govornih virov in tehnologij za slovenski jezik.1 Razpravo, v kateri so sodelujoči raziskovalci govora izpostavili potrebe po večjih količinah raznolikih govornih podatkov iz vsakda­nje, tudi narečne komunikacije, je povezovala izr. prof. dr. Darinka Verdonik. Sodelujoči so opozorili na pomen standardov zapisovanja in označevanja, ki pa morajo biti dobro premišljeni in temeljiti na iz­kušnjah. Strinjali so se, da je govor izhodiščno večmodalen in da ne moremo v analizah izhajati samo iz zapisa govora, ostale modalno­sti pa zanemariti, hkrati pa priznali, da je večmodalnost še vedno problem, za katerega nimamo jasnih rešitev, kako se z njo uspešno raziskovalno soočati. Razpravljali so o kontekstualni vpetosti govora in previdnosti, ki je potrebna pri interpretaciji pomenov, ki izhajajo iz konteksta in o katerih v komunikaciji samo sklepamo. V zadnjem delu so nanizali svoja razmišljanja o najbolj zaželenih aplikacijah go­vornih tehnologij.

title: From AI chatbot-enabled knowledge management to sustainable luxury consumption: the moderating role of need for uniqueness
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how AI chatbot-driven knowledge management, through knowledge acquisition, sharing, and application, influences sustainable luxury fashion consumption. It examines the psychological process from attitude formation to behavior and the moderating role of need for uniqueness. Design/methodology/approach A survey in Ho Chi Minh City collected 446 responses from consumers engaging with chatbots and luxury brands. PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 4) was used for data analysis. Findings Knowledge acquisition and sharing were positively associated with multidimensional attitudes toward sustainable luxury fashion, whereas knowledge application was not significant. Attitude was positively associated with purchase intention and sustainable luxury consumption, while need for uniqueness strengthened the attitude-intention relationship. Originality/value This study extends AI-enabled knowledge management to consumer–brand interactions by integrating differentiated knowledge processes, multidimensional attitudes, and need for uniqueness within the C-A-C framework. The paper provides actionable insights for luxury brands to create personalized, engaging and sustainable consumer experiences.

title: ClothCode: Generative Modeling for Garment State Estimation and Dynamics Prediction
abstract: We introduce ClothCode, a unified generative framework for garment state estimation and action-conditioned dynamics prediction in a shared discrete configuration space. A material-aligned tokenizer encodes garment configuration as residual vector-quantized patch tokens, while task-specific Masked Generative Transformers predict these tokens through parallel confidence-guided refinement. Across three garment templates, ClothCode reduces mean displacement error by 26.6% for state estimation and 37.0% for dynamics prediction relative to the strongest baselines. Dynamics prediction requires only 16.7 ms per window, compared with 556.2 ms for diffusion. Integrated into the same model-predictive controller, ClothCode improves real-world folding and flattening success from 56.7% to 78.9%. Further results and videos are available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/ClothCode-DE32

title: SeoulMMOD: A Large-Scale Multimodal Origin-Destination Flow Benchmark
abstract: Origin-destination (OD) flow forecasting supports urban mobility decisions by predicting the volume and patterns of human movement across a city. Most existing public OD benchmarks provide only a partial view of citywide mobility, covering a single transport service or at most two modes. With partial mode coverage, observed demand changes are difficult to separate into shifts across transport modes and changes in total travel. We introduce SeoulMMOD, a large-scale public benchmark for citywide multimodal mobility in Seoul. SeoulMMOD provides three years of hourly OD flows estimating total mobility for 6 urban travel modes across 25 districts and 426 sub-districts, together with travel-time, travel-distance, calendar, rainfall, and point-of-interest (POI) signals. Using SeoulMMOD, we benchmark 14 forecasting baselines under a common protocol and analyse the effects of spatial scaling, joint versus mode-separate training, and cross-year generalization. Results show that several spatio-temporal models that work at district level do not scale to sub-district OD forecasting, and that naive joint multi-mode training does not consistently improve accuracy. Together, the dataset and benchmark establish a reproducible testbed for multi-mode, multi-year OD forecasting at the city scale.

title: Benchmarking Embedding Geometries and Clustering Algorithms for Unsupervised Patent Claim Classification
abstract: Prior-art retrieval systems are structurally organized around classification codes, making cross-code discovery difficult. This paper asks if an unsupervised representation trained on patent text can recover relevant connections that code-restricted search cannot, and if hyperbolic space helps. We trained a hyperbolic and a matched Euclidean Variational Autoencoder (VAE) on 45,000 US patents (96 runs, 6 seeds). The hyperbolic model retrieves genuinely cross-category prior art 52% more often than the Euclidean model (18.76% vs. 12.34% of top-10 results, 3,000 queries). This represents a practical gain for the motivating search problem. The hyperbolic model agrees less with official classification (NMI 0.2392 vs. 0.3206), which we explain geometrically: the two measures capture different goals, and only one aligns with prior-art search needs. In a study of 10 technology domains (50,000 more patents), we find that a domain's classification breadth--the number of distinct CPC subgroups spanned--predicts approach performance (Pearson r=-0.642, p=0.045, N=10), and that patents per subgroup is an even stronger predictor (r=0.715, p=0.020). This provides a checkable signal for practitioners to determine where the method is most valuable. We report all findings with statistical transparency and release a complete, 91-test automated implementation.

title: Uncertainty-aware automated HER2 scoring via lensfree holography and deep learning
abstract: We present a compact, cost-effective lensfree holographic imager integrated with deep learning for automated HER2 scoring of immunohistochemically stained breast tissue sections. The system captures lensfree diffraction patterns under RGB laser illumination and reconstructs complex optical fields over a large sample area of ~1,250 mm². To enhance diagnostic reliability, we incorporate an uncertainty quantification framework that provides autonomous uncertainty estimates for individual predictions and enables robust HER2 scoring, achieving an error correction rate of 30.4%. Evaluated on a blinded test set of 412 tissue samples, the proposed approach achieves a classification accuracy of 84.9% for 4-class HER2 scoring (0/1+/2+/3+) and 94.8% for binary classification (0/1+ vs. 2+/3+). Despite operating without lenses, mechanical focusing, precision optical alignment, or image registration, this lensfree holographic platform delivers performance comparable to conventional brightfield microscopy–based digital pathology systems, offering a pathway to portable, high-throughput, and cost-effective HER2 scoring, particularly suited to resource-limited settings.

title: Retrieval‐Augmented Lesson Generation With Large Language Models for Scenario‐Based Tutor Training
abstract: ABSTRACT Background High‐impact tutoring can improve student learning, but scaling tutoring programmes requires large numbers of novice tutors. Developing high‐quality tutor‐training lessons remains a key bottleneck. Objectives This study compared post‐test performance after participants studied human‐created or LLM‐created tutor‐training materials and examined whether immediate explanatory feedback moderated differences by lesson creation source (human‐created vs. LLM‐created). Methods We conducted a randomized eight‐condition between‐subjects experiment. Participants completed a source‐matched pre‐instruction practice assessment, studied a tutor‐training lesson created by the same source, and then completed two fixed‐order post‐lesson assessments. The design compared lesson creation source, manipulated immediate explanatory feedback and counterbalanced the pre‐instruction scenario form. Post‐test performance was the mean proportion correct across the human‐created and LLM‐created post‐lesson assessments. Results and Conclusions Average post‐test performance was higher after the human‐created lesson than after the LLM‐created lesson, but this difference depended on feedback. The human‐created advantage appeared in the no‐feedback condition, whereas no statistically reliable lesson creation source difference was detected when feedback was provided. Feedback had no statistically significant overall main effect. The human‐created lesson condition performed better on the human‐created post‐lesson assessment, while the LLM‐created post‐lesson assessment showed a small descriptive difference favouring the LLM‐created lesson condition. Because pre‐instruction performance differed by lesson creation source and scenario form, and because assessment source was confounded with fixed assessment order, the results do not isolate pure learning gains or establish a general transfer advantage.

title: Simple Linear Corrections for Compression in Late Interaction
abstract: Late-interaction (multi-vector) models represent documents using a set of token-level vectors, providing a middle ground between cross-encoders and dense encoders in terms of quality and cost of embedding. However, compared to the latter, the indices are costly to store and score. Pooling and pruning based compression techniques are deployed widely but deteriorate in quality noticeably with aggressive compression. We investigate whether a lightweight change to the scoring function can recover retrieval quality after document-vector compression. For each combination of encoder, compressor, and vector budget, we learn a global linear correction by distilling the uncompressed model's score distributions over candidate documents. The encoder and compressor remain frozen, and the correction can be applied to each query at search time or once, offline, to the stored vectors. We evaluate the method with ColBERTv2 and Jina v4 on MS MARCO and BEIR, and with ColPali2 on the ViDoRe v3 visual document retrieval benchmark. Experiments cover four training-free compression methods, multiple vector budgets, in-domain adaptation, and transfer from MS MARCO to BEIR. In the in-domain setting, the correction improves over baseline compression in 154 of 160 BEIR settings, while transfer from MS MARCO is more variable across models and datasets. We also find that matrices trained with synthetic queries can improve over baseline compression on ViDoRe v3. These results show that a small learned correction can recover some of the quality lost to compression without retraining the encoder or recompressing the documents.

evidence.title: Simple Linear Corrections for Compression in Late Interaction
evidence.abstract: Late-interaction (multi-vector) models represent documents using a set of token-level vectors, providing a middle ground between cross-encoders and dense encoders in terms of quality and cost of embedding. However, compared to the latter, the indices are costly to store and score. Pooling and pruning based compression techniques are deployed widely but deteriorate in quality noticeably with aggressive compression. We investigate whether a lightweight change to the scoring function can recover retrieval quality after document-vector compression. For each combination of encoder, compressor, and vector budget, we learn a global linear correction by distilling the uncompressed model's score distributions over candidate documents. The encoder and compressor remain frozen, and the correction can be applied to each query at search time or once, offline, to the stored vectors. We evaluate the method with ColBERTv2 and Jina v4 on MS MARCO and BEIR, and with ColPali2 on the ViDoRe v3 visual document retrieval benchmark. Experiments cover four training-free compression methods, multiple vector budgets, in-domain adaptation, and transfer from MS MARCO to BEIR. In the in-domain setting, the correction improves over baseline compression in 154 of 160 BEIR settings, while transfer from MS MARCO is more variable across models and datasets. We also find that matrices trained with synthetic queries can improve over baseline compression on ViDoRe v3. These results show that a small learned correction can recover some of the quality lost to compression without retraining the encoder or recompressing the documents.

title: OpenSVBench: Diagnosing Speaker Verification Generalization Across Deployment Scenarios
abstract: Speaker verification (SV) systems now achieve very low error rates on standard public protocols, but those results do not fully describe deployment generalization. VoxCeleb-style evaluations remain useful anchors for English in-the-wild media speech. Scenario-specific evaluations and challenges are also valuable. However, neither setting directly shows whether the same system remains reliable across diverse deployment scenarios. We introduce OpenSVBench, a public benchmark for cross-scenario SV evaluation. Its fixed public core contains 26 trial sets organized into 11 scenario groups, with 9.15M verification trials, frozen target/non-target keys, and metadata for scenario-wise reporting. Around this core, the online leaderboard acts as a diagnostic evaluation interface rather than only a ranked list. It accepts score packages from new systems, evaluates them with frozen keys and common scoring, and reports trial-set breakdowns, scenario-group metrics, macro EER/minDCF, model-wise profiles, and scenario-wise comparisons. We evaluate 18 public checkpoints spanning x-vector, ECAPA-TDNN, CAMPPlus, ResNet and ERes variants, ReDimNet2, SAM-ResNet, and pretrained Transformer speaker recipes. The results show clear cross-scenario gaps: systems with similar macro EER can have different scenario profiles, strong performance in one scenario does not guarantee strong performance in another, and same-scenario trial sets can still expose source and protocol gaps.

title: Sample-Preserving Search-to-Decision Reduction for Noisy Linear Equations over Large Moduli
abstract: The Noisy Linear Equations problem involves finding the solution to a random linear system over a finite field given noisy evaluations. This is a generalisation of various learning problems widely used in cryptography, including Learning with Errors (LWE), Learning with Rounding (LWR), and Learning Parity with Noise (LPN). We present a new sample-preserving search-to-decision reduction for Noisy Linear Equations that has complexity $\mathrm{poly}(n,m,\log q, q/σ)$, where $n$ is the dimension of the secret, $m$ is the number of samples, $q$ is the modulus, and $σ$ is the magnitude of the noise (defined suitably for the kind of noise involved). In particular, this implies search-to-decision reductions for LWE and LWR that run in time $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ even if the modulus $q$ is exponentially large, as long as the noise-to-modulus ratio $σ/q$ is non-negligible. Our reduction works for prime moduli $q$. If $q$ is composite, it instead produces a list that contains a small multiple of the solution. Prior to this work, known search-to-decision reductions for LWE and LWR either did not preserve the parameters of the problem (i.e., $m$, $n$, $σ$, and $q$), or had complexity that scaled polynomially with either $σ$ or the largest prime factor of $q$.

title: Golden Bough Formation Project v1.5: A Complete Design from Branching Optimization to AI Evolution System
abstract: This document establishes the complete theoretical framework and game design loop of the "Golden Bough Formation". Rooted in planar branching optimization (the √2 Theorem) and 3D geometry, it extends to the Crown/Ironwood posture spectrum, four-verb maneuvers (λ-stretch, μ-breathe, rotation, split/merge), and shatter-regeneration mechanics. Covering force deployment from Tree to Forest Stages (Lv1-12), the Apprenticeship System, and Scale Cost principles, it implements an AI Black-Box evolution closed-loop via the "Champion-Challenger Gate" (55% safety line). Validated by a triple-matrix and benchmarked against Free Skirmish AI, it forges a structured combat paradigm that "survives beatings and grows stronger from them". The text is Markdown-native with embedded formulas and figures, including a glossary and validation checklist.

title: Interpretable Causal Structure Learning for Multivariate Air Quality Forecasting: An Integrated Evolutionary-Cognitive Approach
abstract: Accurate Air Quality Index (AQI) forecasting is essential for public health protection and sustainable urban planning. Existing data-driven forecasting models often provide limited interpretability of pollutant interactions, while conventional Fuzzy Cognitive Map (FCM) learning algorithms may struggle to optimize causal weights effectively. To address these limitations, this study proposes IGWO-FCM, an evolutionary-cognitive framework that integrates an Improved Grey Wolf Optimizer (IGWO) with FCMs for interpretable causal structure learning and AQI forecasting under uncertainty. The framework employs FCMs to represent pollutant interactions and feedback mechanisms, and introduces a hierarchical transformation operator and adaptive learning strategy to enhance causal weight optimization. On a real-world urban AQI dataset comprising 744 hourly records and six pollutants, as well as two public benchmarks, IGWO-FCM achieves the lowest MAE and RMSE among the compared FCM learning algorithms for five of the six pollutants, reducing these errors by up to 29.6% and 40.2%, respectively, relative to the strongest baseline. These results demonstrate the predictive performance of IGWO-FCM and its potential to provide interpretable insights into pollutant interactions for AQI forecasting.

title: Amortized Counterfactual Prediction with Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Counterfactual inference asks how an observed outcome might have differed under different circumstances, such as whether a patient would have recovered had they received a different treatment. Such questions arise whenever decisions depend on the outcomes of alternatives that were not observed. Answering counterfactual queries generally requires knowledge of the underlying causal structure, which is often unavailable in practice. A common approach is therefore to first estimate the causal graph from observational data and then perform counterfactual inference. However, errors in the estimated causal graph can propagate to downstream counterfactual predictions. To address this challenge, we introduce the Counterfactual Graph Neural Process (CFGNP), an end-to-end approach that answers counterfactual queries directly from observational data without first estimating a causal graph. CFGNP uses Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to exploit the dual-graph structure by restricting cross-world message passing to corresponding factual--counterfactual variables. Across synthetic and image-based benchmarks, CFGNP achieves stronger predictive performance than existing approaches, including on the German Loan benchmark, where it reduces MSE from $4.51 \times 10^{-2}$ to $0.19 \times 10^{-2}$. Furthermore, on synthetic causal graphs, a model trained only on 10-node graphs maintains strong predictive performance on graphs with up to 30 nodes, without retraining.

title: A Better Metric Will Not Save You: What You Compare Beats How You Compare It
abstract: Representational similarity measures (RSA, CKA, Procrustes) are chosen for the transformations they treat as irrelevant, and all of them take the set of conditions as given. That set is fixed by two decisions, which inputs are admitted and how they are grouped, both taken before the matrix a measure operates on exists: no invariance property reaches them. We measure what they are worth where the arrangement the conditions ought to have is known independently of the systems compared, the acoustic organisation of vowels, across fifteen languages and twenty-seven representations. Changing which categories are compared, at a fixed number of them, moves the gap between two representations by more than twice the effect being measured, while changing how many moves it not at all. In this setting rankings of models are identified under these choices, and rankings across languages are not.

title: Learning Schwarzschild Geodesic Motion with Lagrangian Neural Networks
abstract: Lagrangian Neural Networks (LNNs) learn dynamics from trajectory data by parameterizing a scalar Lagrangian and deriving accelerations through the Euler--Lagrange equation, providing a variational inductive bias that improves physical consistency over purely data-driven models. LNNs have recently been extended to general relativistic settings, leaving Schwarzschild geodesics as an open challenge. Training on complex relativistic systems is hindered by the diversity of the dynamics, as well as numerical instabilities and the difficulty of adequately sampling physically relevant, diverse orbital regimes. We introduce two coordinated improvements: a decoupled position--velocity normalization scheme that independently rescales each coordinate and its time derivatives, reweighting acceleration targets to balance contributions across all channels; and an energy-constrained log-uniformly sampled dataset generation strategy informed by the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) structure. With these improvements, our model accurately reproduces perihelion precession and relativistic time dilation, conserves energy and angular momentum to within a few percent even after completing multiple orbits around the central mass and predicts orbital trajectories across eight orbital scenarios in close, medium, and far-field regimes. These results establish that LNNs, augmented with physically motivated normalization and sampling, can reliably learn geodesic dynamics in curved spacetime. Our work also represents the first successful training of LNNs on Schwarzschild geodesics and offers a promising direction for data-driven modeling of complex relativistic systems.

title: Gaussian-Width Bounds for Offline-to-Online Linear Bandits
abstract: We study how offline data can help online learning in stochastic linear bandits. We focus on partially covered offline data, where only $k$ of the $d$ feature directions are poorly covered. Existing analyses of algorithms based on phased elimination and optimism give regret bounds of order $\widetilde O(\sqrt{dkT})$ in this regime. We show that this dependence arises from loose control of the reward prediction error, and obtain tighter bounds using concentration of Lipschitz functions of Gaussian vectors. Based on this analysis, we develop a phased elimination algorithm with regret $\widetilde O(k\sqrt T)$. For the unit Euclidean ball, we prove a matching regret lower bound under partial coverage, as well as matching upper and lower bounds under uniform offline coverage. We also study pure exploration with offline data, providing algorithms and matching upper and lower bounds on simple regret for fixed-design algorithms and also for adaptive algorithms under partial and uniform coverage of offline data.
