title: The Use of Natural Language Processing (NLP) in the Automated Detection and Correction of Grammatical Errors in Students’ English Writing
abstract: Accurate, timely feedback on grammatical accuracy remains one of the most persistent challenges in English language teaching, particularly in large classes where teacher marking capacity is limited. This article reviews recent developments in the use of natural language processing (NLP) for the automated detection and correction of grammatical errors in students’ English writing. A narrative synthesis of 26 peer-reviewed studies and preprints was combined with an illustrative case study in which a hybrid Transformer–large language model (LLM) pipeline was applied to 240 essays written by EFL undergraduates. The review shows a clear technological trajectory from rule-based and statistical correctors through sequence-to-sequence neural models to pretrained encoders and, most recently, instruction-tuned LLMs capable of generating explanatory feedback. Reported systems now routinely exceed 80% precision on high-frequency error categories such as article and determiner use, although word-order errors and context-dependent preposition choice remain difficult. Pedagogically, automated written corrective feedback (AWCF) improves accuracy and revision behaviour, but over-reliance, uneven coverage of low-frequency errors, and hallucinated corrections by generative models require careful instructional design. The article concludes with implications for integrating NLP tools as formative, teacher-in-the-loop aids rather than stand-alone assessors.

title: GeoShift: a four-survey geochemical benchmark for cross-survey evaluation under detection-limit censoring (data)
abstract: GeoShift is a benchmark for evaluating machine-learning models across geochemical surveys under detection-limit censoring. This record archives its data. Observational arm: harmonised concentrations (mg/kg), left-censoring indicators and per-cell detection limits for 39 primary-core elements in NGSA (Australia, 1,315 samples) and NASGL (conterminous USA, 4,857 samples), with sample identifiers, coordinates, Köppen climate group and GLiM lithology for all 8,285 observational samples. GEMAS (Europe, 2,113 samples) is represented by identifiers, coordinates and fold assignments only; its values are not redistributed and are fetched from the Geological Survey Ireland publication on data.gov.ie by the code record. Controlled arm: Tellus (Ireland and Northern Ireland, 5,643 topsoil samples), with published X-ray fluorescence (XRFS) and aqua-regia ICP values for 47 elements measured by both routes, a left-censoring indicator per route, and limit provenance (38 elements accredited on both routes). Also included: frozen fold assignments (random, spatially blocked, environmentally blocked, leave-one-survey-out, pairwise and predictor-space protocols), element crosswalk, detection-limit tables, censoring audits and SHA-256 checksums. Derived from NGSA (Geoscience Australia, CC BY 4.0), NASGL (U.S. Geological Survey, public domain) and Tellus (Geological Survey Ireland and Geological Survey of Northern Ireland, CC BY 4.0). Cite the original surveys when using these data. Code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23269524 Accompanying article: Sulaiman, D. A., Hassen, S. I., Abdlrazaq, A. A., and Noori, E. M.: GeoShift: a four-survey geochemical benchmark for cross-survey evaluation under detection-limit censoring, Earth System Science Data (in preparation).

title: Certifying quantum non-Gaussianity with an unknown common phase
abstract:
An unknown optical phase can hide quantum non-Gaussianity in every individual mode while leaving it certifiable in the joint light. This paper shows when Gaussian measurements can exclude the complete Gaussian convex hull without knowing the source's common phase, and gives explicit finite-sample tests. The results guide whether to preserve phase relations between emissions and how to process the resulting measurement records. 1. Certification against the full Gaussian model. Let \(\mathcal G_n\) be the trace-norm-closed convex hull of all physical \(n\)-mode Gaussian states. For a fixed known \(ho
otin\mathcal G_1\), form the common-phase state \[\Omega_n=\int_0^{2\pi}(U_\phiho U_\phi^\dagger)^{\otimes n}\, rac{d\phi}{2\pi},\qquad U_\phi=e^{-i\phi N}.\] Finite Gaussian measurements with a laboratory phase reference and bounded classical scores achieve arbitrarily small false-positive and missed-detection probabilities. The null includes arbitrary Gaussian entanglement and classical correlations, with unrestricted displacement, squeezing and energy. title: Coarse-to-Fine Label Distribution Learning for High-Cardinality Survey Simulation
abstract: Modeling fine-grained survey distributions for high-cardinality large language model prediction is challenging under mixed-cardinality supervision. Because low-cardinality surveys dominate training, standard label distribution learning (LDL) develops positional bias toward early response regions and fails to generalize probability allocation to extended spaces. This bias collapses probability mass into low-index regions, thereby fragmenting high-cardinality distributions. To address this, the authors propose hierarchical LDL, a coarse-to-fine framework using macroscopic anchors to calibrate fine-grained predictions. By jointly optimizing hierarchical distributions, hierarchical LDL stabilizes probability allocation across sparsely supervised high-cardinality scales and improves structural alignment.

title: Semantic Edge-Cloud Communication for Real-Time Urban Traffic Digital Twins
abstract: Urban traffic systems are becoming increasingly complex, demanding real-time traffic perception, proactive collision prediction, and intelligent management to improve safety and reduce congestion. Although AI-driven traffic management has shown strong promise, its success relies on diverse, high-quality data spanning critical scenarios such as collisions, near-collisions, and traffic rule violations. Digital twins offer a powerful solution by enabling synchronized virtual replicas of physical traffic environments for real-time monitoring, collision prediction, traffic-flow optimization, and diverse realistic scenario generation. However, continuously synchronizing a high-fidelity urban traffic digital twin through edge surveillance cameras requires substantial edge-cloud communication, and transmitting raw video streams leads to severe bandwidth and latency constraints. To overcome this challenge, this paper proposes a semantic communication-based edge-cloud framework for real-time urban traffic digital twin applications. By leveraging edge intelligence to extract and transmit only task-relevant semantic traffic information instead of full video feeds, the proposed framework significantly reduces communication overhead while preserving the essential dynamics needed for accurate real-time digital twin reconstruction. Experimental results demonstrate more than 99% transmission savings and an average trajectory reconstruction error of only 0.12 m, confirming the proposed framework as an effective, scalable, and low-latency solution for AI-enabled urban traffic digital twin applications.

title: Enhancing Legal Reasoning in Pre-trained Language Models via Knowledge Graph-Guided Multi-Task Pre-training
abstract: Legal language understanding requires reasoning over semi-structured regulatory documents, yet standard pre-training objectives do not explicitly target this structural capability. Because current legal language models rely solely on masked language modeling, they treat statutory text as flat token sequences and ignore the underlying hierarchical constraints. To bridge this gap, we present a multi-task pre-training approach for German traffic law (StVO). Our approach combines three complementary objectives: Next Sentence Prediction (NSP), Knowledge Graph (KG) Guided Clustering (CLU), and Knowledge Graph (KG) Aware Paragraph Classification (CLS). This approach explicitly encodes structured legal knowledge directly into the model weights. This encoding enables zero-shot legal reasoning at inference time and removes the need for discrete graph traversal. We evaluate our approach across nine Transformer-based encoders and 324 experimental runs. On synthetic StVO question answering, our models demonstrate consistent relative improvements between 10.3% and 155.0% over baselines. Furthermore, relative to the established LexGLUE baselines (Chalkidis et al., 2022), our models improve over prior results on four of seven legal benchmarks. It also achieves consistent zero-shot transfer gains between 3.4% and 15.8% on Austrian driving regulations. These experimental results indicate that our training approach generalizes successfully beyond the initial training legal domain.

title: FPD-Drive: Future Policy Distillation for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving models are typically trained on real-world driving logs, which record only the trajectory actually executed in each scene. This provides limited supervision for learning alternative valid behaviors. Multi-target supervision can mitigate this limitation, but broader trajectory coverage makes safe candidate selection more challenging. We propose FPD-Drive, an end-to-end planner that distills privileged future knowledge into a visual driving policy to improve both multi-trajectory supervision and safety selection. Specifically, we introduce Future-Privileged Multi-Target Distillation to transfer diverse, high-quality trajectory targets from a teacher with access to recorded future observations to the student. These targets extend supervision beyond the single recorded human trajectory. For candidate selection, we further introduce Safety-Aware Score Correction to correct ranking errors between nearby safe and unsafe candidates and raise underestimated safety scores of safe candidates. At deployment, the student requires neither future observations nor teacher inference. Our base model achieves 94.9 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 navtest and 55.9 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 navhard. The scaled FPD-Drive-Pro improves these scores to 95.5 PDMS and 58.1 EPDMS, respectively, achieving SOTA performance among the compared methods on both benchmarks. Zero-shot closed-loop evaluation on HUGSIM further yields an HD-Score of 45.1 and RC of 55.3.

title: Sort the Vocabulary: Prefix-Ordered Token Classes Make Two-Level Language-Model Heads Cheap and Faithful — code and experimental results
abstract: Research code, reproducible experiment scripts, raw results, and the preprint on prefix-ordered token classes for two-level language-model output heads. The study compares grouping criteria in five frozen open language models and models trained from scratch, with end-to-end CPU and head-only GPU cost measurements. Among the standard grouping baselines, prefix ordering has the lowest mean KL to the original head in four of five frozen models. At equal head cost, prefix blocks reduce KL by 27–33% relative to the token ordering released for Gemma 4. Sequential one-token-at-a-time CPU scoring of Gemma 3 270M is 2.4× faster with AVX-512 and 2.1× with AVX2; GPU measurements cover the output head only. Likelihood and KL results are limited to the text domains described in the paper; downstream tasks and speculative-decoding acceptance were not evaluated. The variations study includes a word-start/continuation hybrid, reversed-spelling controls, three-level trees, block-size sweeps, and a failed refinement heuristic. This version archives repository commit 786f36adfdd868abd69c9069336f18d955728b85. Code, results and the preprint are included in prefix-head-1.0.zip; main.pdf is also provided separately.

title: Asymmetric Sending-or-Not-Sending Twin-Field Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: We propose an improved protocol that combines the code-bit option [z] of the Universal SNS framework with asymmetric sending probabilities across odd-indexed and even-indexed time windows. This approach increases the fraction of single-sided events that contribute to the raw key, while the [z] option ensures that all heralded events involving the signal and vacuum intensities are retained as code bits. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed protocol significantly outperforms both the SNS protocol with actively odd-parity pairing (SNS-AOPP) and the Universal SNS protocol with the [x, y, z] option. At a secret key rate of 1 kbps, the proposed protocol extends the maximum secure distance by 103.7 km compared to SNS-AOPP. The key rate improvement reaches more than a factor of 11 over the entire distance range, and this result shows that the combination of the [z] option with asymmetric sending probabilities provides a simple yet effective means of enhancing the performance of SNS-TF-QKD without requiring changes to the quantum hardware.

title: Convergence Theory for Deep and Multi-grade Neural Architectures
abstract: This dissertation studies two complementary notions of convergence arising in modern neural network models: the convergence of recursively constructed neural network architectures and the convergence of optimization algorithms used for training neural-network-based image restoration models. The first part develops a convergence theory for deep neural networks (DNNs) viewed as recursively generated sequences of functions. Within an Lp framework motivated by statistical learning, sufficient conditions are established under which increasing-depth neural network sequences converge to well-defined limiting functions. The analysis covers both bounded-width and unbounded-width architectures, establishes explicit convergence rates, and motivates a network initialization strategy derived from the convergence conditions. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical predictions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed initialization. The second part extends the analysis to multi-grade deep neural networks (MGDNNs), whose hierarchical construction naturally generates sequences of neural network approximations. Separate convergence theories are developed for free-weight and shared-weight formulations, and sufficient conditions are established for pointwise, uniform, and Lp convergence under general Lipschitz continuous activation functions. These results provide a rigorous characterization of the asymptotic behavior of multi-grade neural architectures as the number of grades increases. The final part considers a multi-grade sparse-guided implicit representation model for training-data-free image restoration. Unlike the preceding chapters, the convergence studied here concerns the optimization algorithm used to compute the network parameters. A fixed-point formulation of the associated proximal alternating algorithm is derived, and convergence to stationary points is established under suitable regularity assumptions. Together, these results develop new theoretical foundations for recursively constructed DNNs, hierarchical MGDNNs, and optimization methods for training-data-free image restoration.

title: Advanced optical quantum computing using liquid crystal devices
abstract: Liquid crystal (LC) devices are primarily used in display applications due to their characteristics of thinness, light weight, large area, and low driving voltage. We are studying optical quantum computing using the optical rotation and large phase control properties of LCs. In this paper, we would like to review the latest developments in this subject. First, we investigated the Young’s double-slit experiment using self-alignment LC devices in order to minimize misalignment. A fully logical “NOT” operation of the interfered Sinc and cosine function was achieved. Second, we investigate Mach– Zehnder interferometric photon-count control with extremely weak light, which was conducted using the nematic and ferroelectric LC device. By applying voltage, the average photon counts were statistically controlled between single-photon and 197-photon levels, and changes consistent with the Poisson and Gaussian distributions were confirmed. Third, multi-bit optical-path linear quantum computing using the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm with the twisted nematic LC device as a linear optical element was demonstrated. For the 4-bit linear optical quantum computing case, the optical intensities are in good agreement with the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm; the fidelity of the “uniform” case is 98.7%. The results of the expansion to 6 bits were also demonstrated. One of the merits of this linear quantum computing is large-scale scalability, as high-resolution display panels are being mass-produced. These studies are promising for photonic quantum computing with a new era of technology.

title: State-Isolated Vision Mamba via Update-Tendency Routing for Underwater Image Enhancement
abstract: Vision Mamba has recently emerged as an efficient alternative to convolutional and Transformer-based architectures by modeling long-range spatial dependencies through recurrent state evolution. Existing studies primarily improve token serialization, scanning strategies, or expert routing, yet largely overlook a state level question question: how should recurrent states be organized for spatially heterogeneous visual restoration? In this paper, we show that forcing tokens with heterogeneous update behaviors to recurrently modify a shared hidden state leads to persistent cross-content interference, which we term \textbf{State Contention}. We further argue that effective recurrent modeling should organize state evolution according to token compatibility rather than token ordering. Based on this observation, we introduce \textbf{State Isolation}, a new recurrent state organization principle for Vision Mamba,tokens with compatible state-update tendencies evolve within independent recurrent state streams. To instantiate this principle, we propose \textbf{IsoMamba}, a $Δ$-guided architecture that constructs model-intrinsic update representations, discovers update-compatible token groups through label-free clustering, and routes them to isolated Mamba experts following a \textbf{cluster--route--isolate} paradigm. In addition, we develop a dynamic channel-wise reweighting objective to compensate for wavelength-dependent reconstruction difficulty in underwater images. Extensive experiments demonstrate that IsoMamba consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple underwater image enhancement benchmarks while providing cleaner hidden state responses, validating the effectiveness of state isolated recurrent modeling.

title: NEAR: Neighborhood-Aware Residuals for Memory Retrieval
abstract: Memory retrieval aims to identify evidence from stored records to answer a query. Stored records with different factual details may share topics, entities, or events. Such shared contents would make records without the required evidence more likely to receive high similarity scores and outrank the correct evidence. In this paper, we use the information shared by these records to construct local references for query-memory matching. We propose NEighborhood-Aware Residuals (NEAR), a training-free framework that uses these references to construct residual representations that complement the original embeddings. Specifically, each memory derives a reference direction from its neighbors, and each query obtains its reference from a precomputed table. Using these references, NEAR constructs projection residuals for both queries and memories. These residuals are combined with the original embeddings for a single approximate nearest-neighbor search over a fixed memory index. Experiments on eight long-context retrieval benchmarks show consistent improvements across nine embedding models. Downstream evaluations show that NEAR improves question-answering performance.

evidence.title: NEAR: Neighborhood-Aware Residuals for Memory Retrieval
evidence.abstract: Memory retrieval aims to identify evidence from stored records to answer a query. Stored records with different factual details may share topics, entities, or events. Such shared contents would make records without the required evidence more likely to receive high similarity scores and outrank the correct evidence. In this paper, we use the information shared by these records to construct local references for query-memory matching. We propose NEighborhood-Aware Residuals (NEAR), a training-free framework that uses these references to construct residual representations that complement the original embeddings. Specifically, each memory derives a reference direction from its neighbors, and each query obtains its reference from a precomputed table. Using these references, NEAR constructs projection residuals for both queries and memories. These residuals are combined with the original embeddings for a single approximate nearest-neighbor search over a fixed memory index. Experiments on eight long-context retrieval benchmarks show consistent improvements across nine embedding models. Downstream evaluations show that NEAR improves question-answering performance.

title: ReSFlow: Rectifying Categorical Flows on Statistical Manifolds for One-Step Generation
abstract: Generative modeling for discrete data has been significantly advanced by learning continuous vector fields on the statistical manifolds to transport simple priors to target discrete distributions. However, because these continuous-time flows are not constrained to follow geodesics on the statistical manifold, thereby requiring multi-step numerical integration for simulation and leading to substantial computational costs during inference. In this work, drawing inspiration from the "straight and fast" properties of Rectified Flow in continuous Euclidean space, we propose the Rectified Statistical Flow (ReSFlow) model, which enables one-step categorical generation on statistical manifolds by explicitly learning geodesic trajectories that adhere to the intrinsic Riemannian geometry. By rectifying the flow on the statistical manifold, we theoretically guarantee that trajectories between prior and target distributions approximate geodesics. This rectification significantly reduces the transport cost by aligning the learned trajectories directly along geodesics on the statistical manifold, allowing the model to map pure noise to target discrete data in a single step. Through extensive experiments on diverse real-world generative tasks, ranging from image and text to biological domains, we demonstrate ReSFlow's superior one-step generation quality, which truly embodies geodesically optimal and rapid categorical generation. Our code is available at https://github.com/xiaohuanjia/ReSFlow.

title: Hamiltonian-Aware ADAPT Variational Quantum Eigensolver for Molecular Ground-State Simulation
abstract: Abstract Designing compact ansätze for the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) is crucial for calculating energies of large molecules on near-term quantum devices. However, the widely used Adaptive Derivative-Assembled Pseudo-Trotter (ADAPT) ansätze present two challenges: the inherent locality of conventional criteria results in inappropriate excitation operator selection, and the inevitable degradation of certain operators gives rise to redundant accumulation. In this paper, we propose the Hamiltonian-Aware (HA) ADAPT-VQE algorithm to address these issues. First, we present a novel excitation operator selection criterion, which overcomes the locality constraint of existing criteria by incorporating Hamiltonian information. It effectively avoids selecting ineffective operators by prioritizing physically meaningful ones, and incurs no extra classical or quantum computational overhead. Second, we develop a new problem-adaptive method for discriminating and pruning redundant excitation operators stemming from improper selection and inevitable degradation. This method balances redundant operator pruning and convergence guarantee, and is applicable to ansätze with arbitrary scales. Systematic numerical experiments on typical strongly correlated molecular systems demonstrate that our HA-ADAPT-VQE mitigates energy plateaus and outperforms baseline algorithms in terms of energy error, ansatz size, and measurement cost in most cases. This work offers an efficient, robust ansatz construction paradigm, facilitating the development and practical deployment of large-scale VQE in quantum chemistry.

title: Code and Artifacts for "Is Low-Pass Pre-Filtering a Free Lunch? Trade-offs and a Noise-Aware Calibration Alternative in Reconstruction-Based Sensor Anomaly Detection"
abstract: This repository contains the official code, experimental protocols, synthetic fault injection pipelines, and evaluation artifacts for the paper: **"Is Low-Pass Pre-Filtering a Free Lunch? Trade-offs and a Noise-Aware Calibration Alternative in Reconstruction-Based Sensor Anomaly Detection"**. AbstractLow-pass pre-filtering is a common heuristic for suppressing high-frequency hardware noise before reconstruction-based anomaly detection on edge sensors. This work investigates the trade-offs of this practice and proposes a filter-free alternative. Evaluating five pre-processing methods across six detectors on an industrial temperature series from the Numenta Anomaly Benchmark (NAB), we demonstrate that pre-filtering attenuates short transient events, degrades AUPRC, and introduces significant detection latency. Furthermore, we show that reconstruction models on unfiltered data already achieve near-perfect separability (AUPRC ≈ 1.000); their failure during noise bursts is a threshold calibration issue rather than a separability failure. As a zero-latency alternative, we introduce **Noise-Aware Conformal Calibration (NACC)**, which dynamically scales alarm thresholds using a causal median-absolute-deviation (MAD) local noise estimate calibrated via Mondrian split-conformal prediction. NACC lowers the autoencoder's false-alarm rate inside noise bursts to 5.7% while retaining 100% event recall with zero added filter latency. Artifact Contents- `data/`: Processed NAB industrial temperature segments under strict leakage-free temporal splitting protocols.- `src/filters/`: Exact impulse response and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) analytical scripts for Butterworth and moving average filters.- `src/models/`: PyTorch implementations for MaxDev, PCA, Isolation Forest, Dense Autoencoder (674 params), Variational Autoencoder (VAE), and MC-Dropout Autoencoder.- `src/calibration/`: Causal MAD noise estimator and Mondrian split-conformal thresholding algorithm.- `experiments/`: Benchmark evaluation scripts, seed iteration runners, and Bayesian-bootstrap interval generators

title: Code and results for "Cryptanalysis of Chained-Diffusion and Permutation-Only Image Ciphers, and Format-Preserving Authenticated Encryption for Palette Images"
abstract: Python code and result files accompanying the manuscript "Cryptanalysis of Chained-Diffusion and Permutation-Only Image Ciphers, and Format-Preserving Authenticated Encryption for Palette Images" (under review). Contents:- FP-SIV, the proposed format-preserving authenticated encryption scheme for palette images, its file version for real PNG-8 and GIF files (frames, transparency, ancillary data), known-answer test vectors, and its evaluation.- Re-implementations of three published image ciphers (Huang et al. 2025; Kılıç and Kasapbaşı 2025; Jackson and Perumal 2026) and the attacks that break them.- Chosen-plaintext and ciphertext-only attacks on permutation-only palette ciphers.- Structural analyses of the studied substitution-diffusion chain (exhaustive differential and linear tables, weak-key test, locality).- Scripts that regenerate the tables of the manuscript, and the JSON result files they read.- Scripts that rebuild the corpus of 700 real web palette files from the Internet Archive (file list with SHA-256 digests; the files themselves are not redistributed). Test images (USC-SIPI, Kodak, Enrico) are not included; the README explains how to obtain them. Requirements: Python 3.11+, numpy, scipy, pillow, numba, cryptography, gmpy2, matplotlib, scikit-image. See README.md for the script-to-table mapping.

title: "Предикат тождества природы вещей: дедуктивный подход к верификации структурного соответствия описания и генезиса" title_alternate: "Predicate of Identity: A Deductive Approach to Verification of Structural Correspondence Between Description and Genesis"
abstract: The predicate of identity method presents a deductive approach to verification of structural correspondence between a description of an entity (D) and its genesis — the nature of the thing (G). Unlike existing probabilistic methods (NLI, FEVER, RAG) that compare text to text, the proposed method compares description to reality through a four-component tuple (E, V, M, Σ) describing any entity regardless of its nature. The method introduces an axiological scale of 11 anomaly types, proven by a completeness theorem: the space of discrepancies D × G is exhausted by eleven types, ordered by the degree of identity violation — from data substitution (I) to emergent insufficiency (XI). Five operation modes (auto, direct, inverse, emergent, full) provide adaptive verification under conditions of incomplete or excessive description. The architecture includes an LLM adapter that delegates only the parsing of free text into a structured tuple to the language model, while verification remains deterministic. LLM hallucinations during parsing are detected by the core as anomalies — the principle "LLM = parsing, core = truth." Validation was conducted at six levels: 1,000,000 synthetic cases, 8 real cases on regulatory documents (FNP), 1,000 cross-domain cases across 10 subject areas, 55 foundational cases (Darwin's theory, the Bible, modern science vs. nature of things), 30 targeted cases for activating rare types, and 5,000 LLM validation cases. Result: 11 out of 11 types activated, 0 new types, 0 crashes, accuracy/precision/recall = 100%. Performance — 133,731 cases/sec on CPU without GPU, which is 130 times faster than BERT-based NLI. The method is applicable to any entity — process, thing, or phenomenon of the physical world — from subatomic interactions to social systems. keywords: - predicate of identity - deductive verification - structural correspondence - NLP - LLM validation - emergent insufficiency - anomaly detection - completeness theorem - axiological scale - deterministic NLP - hallucination detection

title: Explainable Deep Learning for Skin Disorder Classification in Resource-Constrained Settings
abstract: Skin conditions are among the most common reasons patients seek medical attention worldwide, ranging from self-limiting infections to chronic, disfiguring, or malignant disease. Although deep learning models for dermatological image classification frequently report high overall accuracy, this metric often conceals critical performance failures on clinically vulnerable minority classes such as cancer. To address this, we propose a hybrid classification framework combining DenseNet121 and EfficientNetB0 architectures with transformer-based feature fusion, trained on a DermNet-derived corpus of clinical photographs. Furthermore, we implement a multi-method post- hoc explainability protocol comparing input-gradient saliency, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME). The framework was evaluated on a held-out test set of 897 images, measuring overall accuracy, balanced accuracy, and cancer recall alongside cross- method attribution consistency on misclassified cases. The results demonstrate that a high overall accuracy of 91.0% masked a severe cancer recall deficit of 40.0%, whereas multi-method explainability exposed shortcut learning vulnerabilities, with SHAP partially attributing decisions to image watermarks. This work contributes evidence that single-number accuracy and single-method explanations are insufficient, and it supports disaggregated performance reporting and multi-method explanation as minimum requirements for reliable clinical artificial intelligence (AI) evaluation

title: Systems, theory, and computers
abstract: Is there a real (dynamical) physical system that is not nonlinear? Probably not. The boundedness of energy and matter sources available for system operation cause the limitation of nonlinearity. There are often geometric and kinematic limitations. The path and its length of every displacement are limited. The maximal speed and acceleration of every technical object are bounded. Some physical processes are inherently nonlinear (e.g., friction). Sophisticated control algorithms are mainly nonlinear. Linear control algorithms cannot ensure a finite reachability time . The study of nonlinear dynamical systems has been attracting more and more research efforts. Their study is challenging owing to their complexity and for their theoretical and practical importance.

title: A Real-World CAD Segmentation Benchmark: Comparing Rule-Based and Learning-Based Approaches through Hole Detection
abstract: CAD segmentation datasets are predominantly synthetic or automatically labelled, leaving it unclear how well existing methods transfer to real-world engineering tasks. Fastener-relevant hole detection represents one such task, requiring human annotation and exhibiting greater geometric complexity than commonly used benchmarks. We address this gap through three main contributions. First, we develop two task-specific rule-based methods, one graph-wire-search and one multi-view based, and complement them with a human-annotated benchmark dataset derived from engineering CAD data that also enables training of UV-Net and AAGNet, representative learning-based approaches for B-Rep segmentation. Second, we conduct an extensive experimental study including parameter optimisation, evaluation on our benchmark dataset, cross-domain generalisation on a synthetic dataset, and an assessment of the feasibility of the approaches at varying dataset sizes and IoU thresholds. Third, we provide evidence-based insights into the strengths and limitations of different approaches: rule-based methods generalise well without training data, with the graph-wire-search method favouring recall and the multi-view method favouring precision, whereas learning-based methods achieve strong performance with sufficient annotations but exhibit reduced robustness under domain shift. These findings highlight trade-offs between data requirements, and robustness, and provide guidance not only for hole detection, but more broadly for real-world CAD segmentation tasks.

title: Automated Detection and Encoding of Cartographic Signs in Historical Maps
abstract: Symbols and icons in archival maps represent an expansive source of evidence for historical geography. In this paper, we present a two-stage framework for (1) detecting cartographic signs in historical maps and (2) generating interpretable sign embeddings that capture both semantics and stylistic variations. We also introduce CaSiDD, an open benchmark dataset spanning multiple sign categories and diverse cartographic styles, designed for generic sign detection. Using YOLOv10-X, we demonstrate the practicality of automated sign detection on historical maps. We then present strategies for creating contrasted, informative embeddings of cartographic signs. We approach embedding design systematically, maximizing expressiveness while suppressing digitization or background material confounders. Our final method, based on an adapted RADIOv4 backbone, effectively encodes both sign form and semantics, while producing interpretable representations. This work lays a foundation for scalable evidence extraction for the comparative study of map signs within cartographic culture and geohistorical research.

title: All-optical deconvolution via quantum cross-correlation spectroscopy with bright twin beams
abstract: The resolution of spectroscopic measurements is fundamentally limited by the convolution between a system's intrinsic response and the instrument response function, creating an ill-posed inverse problem. While entangled photons can theoretically bypass these limits, low photon flux has hindered their experimental realization. Here, we propose quantum cross-correlation spectroscopy (QCCS), utilizing macroscopic twin beams (signal and idler beams) to physically circumvent this convolution limit in coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering. Employing the signal beam as a broadband probe, QCCS achieves all-optical deconvolution through a correlation-enhanced sum-frequency generation channel between the convoluted anti-Stokes and idler beams. By subtracting the uncorrelated background using a 500-femtosecond temporal window, we successfully retrieve narrow Raman bands (8 cm^{-1} and 15 cm^{-1}) completely obscured by a 75 cm^{-1} probe bandwidth without numerical deconvolution or prior knowledge. Our results establish macroscopic quantum correlations as a robust resource for high-fidelity spectroscopy, paving the way for ultrashort-pulse-free operando studies under natural, incoherent excitation conditions.

title: Emo-BPO: Emotion Bidirectional Preference Optimization for Diffusion-based Emotional TTS
abstract: Diffusion-based TTS has demonstrated strong capability in emotional speech generation. However, existing emotion alignment methods primarily reinforce target emotional expressions while overlooking modeling of competing emotional modes, limiting fine-grained controllability. This issue becomes more pronounced under classifier-free guidance (CFG), which relies on contrasting conditional trajectories to shape generation. We propose Emotion Bidirectional Preference Optimization (Emo-BPO), a simple effective framework that jointly learns emotion-aligned and emotion-contrastive score functions from reordered same-text emotional pairs. Our method requires neither auxiliary reward models nor additional annotations, and can be seamlessly integrated into existing diffusion-based TTS systems to improve emotional controllability and expressiveness.

title: FaciliTrain: Practicing Facilitation Skills through AI-Simulated Group Dialogue
abstract: Skilled facilitation supports inclusive small-group dialogue, but deliberate practice is hard to scale: it depends on expert coaches, live practice partners, and iterative feedback. We present FaciliTrain, a voice-based training system in which learners step into the facilitator role of an AI-simulated multi-participant conversation, apply five evidence-based techniques, and receive structured AI feedback to support reflection. We report findings from a mixed-methods study with 24 participants, conducted as a formative study (N = 12) and a controlled pilot (N = 12; 6 treatment, 6 control). Both conditions achieved comparable accuracy on a live evaluation task, though treatment participants' self-rated comfort declined significantly while control participants' comfort improved (p = .018). Reflexive thematic analysis identifies four themes: the taxonomy externalizes implicit facilitation intuitions; Making Connections is the most cognitively demanding technique; voice acts as a deliberate-response forcing function; and participants overwhelmingly preferred AI feedback over self-practice. We discuss design implications for voice-based, AI-supported interpersonal skill training at scale.

title: Systemic Principle Qualification (SPQ)
abstract: AbstractThe central problem addressed by this paper is the epistemic and systemic boundary betweenrepeated functional regularity and a generalized functional principle. A rule, signal, functionalbehavior, or criterion-mediated regularity may occur repeatedly within a system, yet repetition alonedoes not establish that the regularity constitutes a general functional principle of that system. Theproposed Systemic Principle Qualification (SPQ) framework therefore treats principle status as aqualification problem rather than as an assumption of universality.The framework is deliberately problem-centered. Its primary object is the question of what conditionsmust be satisfied before a repeatedly observed regularity can be classified as a generalized functionalprinciple relative to a defined system, criterion, and implementation medium. title: The Learnable Delta Method: Bridging Classical Error Propagation and Deep Learning Optimization
abstract: Uncertainty propagation studies how noise in input data affects the final output of a model. For neural networks, this is essential for making reliable decisions in critical contexts, yet current methods for obtaining uncertainties are often restricted by post-hoc inference or architectural rigidity, while sampling-based methods are computationally demanding. To address these limitations, we extend the Delta method from a traditional post-hoc tool to a learnable component integrated into the loss function. Utilizing a first-order Taylor expansion, we approximate the output variance as a learnable target, enabling the network to adjust its weights during training to achieve accurate variance propagation. We evaluated this Learnable Delta method across various neural network architectures, including Multi-Layer Perceptrons, autoencoders, Convolutional Neural Networks, and Transformers. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves significantly faster processing times compared to sampling-based methods. Furthermore, while alternative analytical methods suffer from catastrophic underconfidence on complex and attention-based structures, our framework maintains stable variance control, tight interval calibration, and excellent cross-dataset generalizability, offering a robust and scalable solution for high-dimensional deep learning tasks.

title: Arabic Multimodal Dataset for Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) has attracted growing interest among researchers in recent years, as multimodal user-generated content (e.g., text and images) has become increasingly common on the Internet. In Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA), multimodal data can provide complementary information to text by capturing aspect-related information across text and image modalities. However, to the best of our knowledge, no existing study has addressed Multimodal Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (MABSA) for Arabic user-generated content using paired text and images. To address this gap, we constructed and annotated Arabic Multimodal Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (AraMABSA), a new Arabic MABSA dataset comprising 1721 Arabic hotel reviews associated with 3653 images collected from Booking.com for hotels located in Saudi Arabia and covering six aspect categories. We developed a human annotation pipeline with well-defined annotation guidelines, structured into three stages adopted from prior MABSA research: text annotation, image annotation, and text–image annotation. We further conducted a systematic validation procedure to evaluate the quality and reliability of the annotated labels, using Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA). Finally, we performed technical validation of the constructed dataset using Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct with supervised Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning for Aspect Category Detection (ACD) and Aspect-Based Sentiment Polarity Classification (ASPC) under text-only and text+images conditions. The IAA results demonstrated strong agreement among the annotators, supporting the consistency of the annotation process and guidelines. The experimental results further showed that the dataset supports learnable ACD and ASPC tasks under the evaluated setup. Text+images increased Macro-F1 from 0.6865 to 0.8761 for ACD and from 0.8257 to 0.8837 for ASPC. For ACD, both input conditions were evaluated against the final text–image reference annotations, with the larger text+images advantage occurring for aspects added during text–image annotation. For ASPC, sentiment labels were derived from the text; therefore, the observed text–image improvement should be interpreted within this annotation design. These findings provide initial technical validation of the AraMABSA dataset and support its use as a resource for future Arabic MABSA research.

title: After the Edit, Freshness and Access Control of Tool-Calling Retrieval and Vector RAG for a Community-Edited Knowledge Base
abstract: Community knowledge bases change, as editors correct records, unpublish drafts and hide prices. An assistant grounded through tool calls to a live, gated data interface should give the new value at the next question and never reveal gated content, whereas vector retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) serves what its index copied until the index is updated. We test both expectations on the knowledge base of a Greek–English agricultural platform on Kythera, Greece, with Claude Haiku 4.5 as router and answer model. Forty-eight counterfactual edits were probed within the conversation that had given the old value and in new conversations before and after a scheduled re-index, and 48 synthetic canary records with unique markers were probed while gated, while visible and after revocation. In new conversations after an edit, a reconstruction of the platform's tool agent gave the new value in 91.7% of cases, RAG with immediate index updates in 95.8% and RAG with batch re-indexing in none before the re-index. Challenged in the conversation that had given the old value, the tool agent gave the new value in 88.4% of conversations, but RAG with immediate index updates, which retrieves with the latest message alone, only in 19.6%, usually withdrawing its earlier answer even when it had been right. The tool agent disclosed gated content in none of 240 probes, whereas batch-indexed RAG disclosed every revoked canary until the re-index and an indexer that ignored the gating flags disclosed gated content in 93 of 96 probes. Freshness depends on the conversation as well as the index, and gating must be enforced wherever content is copied.

title: A grayscale ultrasound-based two-stage deep learning framework for automatic segmentation and benign-malignant differentiation of subpleural pulmonary lesions
abstract: Abstract Background Lung cancer is one of the most lethal malignancies globally. However, accurately differentiating subpleural malignant lesions from benign infectious conditions via grayscale ultrasound remains difficult due to operator subjectivity. We developed and validated a two-stage deep learning framework for automated lesion segmentation and benign-malignant classification. Materials and methods In this retrospective study, the research data were derived from patients with SPLs who attended Center 1 between Jan 2023–Dec 2024, as well as patients recruited from Center 2 and Center 3 Jun 2024–Dec 2024 (serving as External Test Set 1 and 2, respectively). The nnU-Net, U-Net and DeepLabv3 + models were adopted for lesion segmentation, while the DenseNet121/201, EfficientNet-B0/B1/B2/B3/B4/B5, ResNet18/50/101, Inception-V3 and VGG19 models were used for benign-malignant classification. Model performance was evaluated using metrics including the Dice similarity coefficient and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Diagnostic performance of 6 radiologists (3 junior, 3 senior) with varying experience was compared between unaided and AI-assisted readings; pooled three-reader differences were estimated by case-cluster bootstrap with Bonferroni adjustment. Results A total of 1059 patients were included in the study (61.32 ± 13.82 years; 726 male patients). The nnU-Net model achieved optimal segmentation (Dice: 0.920 [tuning-validation set, n = 257], 0.913 [External Test Set 1, n = 108], 0.915 [External Test Set 2, n = 94]). Among thirteen candidate classification architectures, DenseNet121 yielded the best performance on the internal tuning-validation set and was therefore selected as the final model; it was then evaluated on two external cohorts, achieving AUCs of 0.889 (95% CI: 0.827–0.951) and 0.865 (95% CI: 0.790–0.940) in External Test Sets 1 and 2, respectively. Overall diagnostic accuracy was significantly higher in the AI-assisted reading session for junior radiologists in both external test cohorts (both Bonferroni- adjusted P < 0.001), whereas improvements among senior radiologists did not reach statistical significance after multiplicity adjustment. Conclusion The deep learning model constructed in this study can accurately realize automatic segmentation and benign-malignant classification of SPL ultrasound images, serving as a potential auxiliary diagnostic tool. Trial registration Not applicable.

title: What to Know About AI
abstract: AI promises significant increases in efficiency and insight but also brings uncertainty and disruption. Throughout history, executives leading major technological changes have often lacked in-depth expertise in the innovations shaping their industries. The authors begin with a short history of artificial intelligence. The modern AI renaissance began around 2012, triggered by three converging factors: exponential growth in computing power, the explosion of available digital data, and breakthroughs in machine learning algorithms. Building on the circulatory system of data and algorithms, we now turn to the specialized technologies that comprise AI's functional architecture: its “perspective models”. Just as human organs perform specialized functions while contributing to overall health, each AI perspective model addresses different business needs. A living enterprise is organized around three principles that mirror biological systems: distributed sensing, local adaptation with global coherence, and continuous adaptation.

title: When MLLMs miss what humans read: diagnosing and learning to read squint text
abstract: Multimodal LLMs can fail to read text embedded in an image's coarse structure (text a human recovers by squinting) and report that no text is present. We name this class Squint Text and study it as a recognition deficiency, motivated by cases from a production moderation pipeline. We introduce SquintBench, comprising 1076 production-derived moderation images, and SquintCtrl, a controlled synthetic suite for mechanism diagnosis. Frozen-weight analysis shows that hidden text leaves a coarse signal while glyph identity is weakly represented; identity becomes substantially more accessible when the correct spatial regions are supplied, implicating spatial selection as a major bottleneck. Suppressing high-frequency content also improves reading at a fixed visual-token budget, while visual token count may also contribute. These findings motivate Squint OPSD: a frozen teacher receives a downscaled view and the ground-truth transcription as privileged context, and its token-level distributions supervise a student along on-policy trajectories. At inference, the student reads the original image alone. Squint OPSD reaches 88.61 ANLS on SquintBench, versus 26.50 for the unadapted backbone, 24.44 for the best general-purpose model on the original view, and 68.60 at best for an off-the-shelf model under a downscaled view. These results substantially narrow the gap between available visual evidence and its generated read-out without auxiliary views at inference.

title: EndoRSI: Physical-Evidence-Driven Recursive Improvement of Endoscopic Robot Policies
abstract: Artificial intelligence is beginning to automate scientific discovery, yet physical robot-policy research still relies on scientists and engineers to interpret experimental failures and decide how controllers should be revised. We present EndoRSI (Endoscopic Recursive Self-Improvement), a human-governed, self-improving robotic research system in which the embedded EndoForge coding agent iteratively develops and refines endoscopic robot policies using evidence from physical experiments. Physical execution remains isolated within a safety-constrained runtime under human authorisation. In motorised endoscopy, validation evidence first caused the agent to reject an initial action representation, while subsequent physical experiments falsified an offline-supported insertion strategy by revealing hazardous closed-loop behaviour absent from the source data. Failed physical rollouts were then incorporated into policy revision; insertion success subsequently increased from 2/21 in the first generation to 17/21 in the fourth. The frozen final policy retained competence across visual and hardware shifts and was the best performing autonomous policy across six independent ex-vivo porcine specimens. These results show that physical robot interaction can serve as experimental evidence for agent-driven robot policy research.

title: Tensor-based Fusion of Multi-modal Data for Predicting Cancer Risk Levels
abstract: Cancer diagnosis and treatment increasingly rely on multi-modal diagnostic technologies that generate high-dimensional datasets. Although these datasets are rich in pathological information, they pose considerable challenges in interpretation, dimensionality reduction, and clinical applicability. Conventional machine learning approaches often fail to extract meaningful cross-modal features, thereby limiting predictive accuracy in patient risk stratification. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an unsupervised machine learning framework that integrates feature extraction, tensor decomposition, and clustering to improve cancer risk prediction. The framework employs tensor decomposition to fuse heterogeneous genomic and clinical data, enabling the extraction of latent, biologically meaningful features that outperform unimodal feature sets. Multiple feature extraction strategies are investigated, and the resulting features are subsequently clustered using a range of clustering algorithms. Comparative evaluations based on internal and external metrics are then used to identify the most effective configurations. The framework is validated on LinkedOmics data comprising 11,158 patients across 32 cancer types. For patient risk stratification, clinically relevant attributes such as tumor purity, pathological stage, and survival outcomes serve as ground-truth indicators. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of tSVD+GMM, which consistently outperforms other configurations across clinical benchmarks.

title: NucleoNet: A Nuclear-Aware Determinant Ansatz for Multi-Geometry Neural Variational Monte Carlo
abstract: Neural-network variational Monte Carlo provides an accurate route to solving the electronic Schrödinger equation, but many neural wavefunctions are optimized for a single nuclear geometry, requiring separate calculations to map out a potential energy surface. We introduce NucleoNet, a nuclear-aware determinant ansatz in which electrons and nuclei form a unified particle set propagated through a shared electron--nucleus backbone that jointly evolves one-particle and two-particle representations. Nuclei carry learned representations that evolve alongside the electronic representations and condition orbital construction, while antisymmetry is imposed only by electronic determinants. On equilibrium small-molecule benchmarks, NucleoNet achieves accuracy comparable to established neural-wavefunction baselines with substantially fewer parameters. For each molecular system, a single model optimized jointly across geometries describes the N$_2$ dissociation curve, Li displacement in LiCN, and the ethane and formamide minimum-energy paths for bond dissociation. Sparse-geometry training generalizes to unseen geometries for N$_2$ and LiCN without further optimization, and N$_2$ ablations show that nuclear streams substantially improve this interpolation. These results show that a compact wavefunction with jointly evolved nuclear representations can describe the geometries of a molecular system with a single set of parameters.

title: QuantumShield AI: An AI-Powered Post-Quantum Cryptography Recommendation Platform
abstract: The finalization of the NIST post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205), with FN-DSA (draft FIPS 206), has shifted the migration question from whether to adopt PQC to which standard best fits an organization's operational and regulatory context. Existing studies benchmark these algorithms thoroughly but stop short of a selection mechanism, leaving practitioners to interpret timing tables by hand. This paper presents QuantumShield AI, a decision-support platform that formalizes PQC algorithm selection as a multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) problem, encodes the selection task as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO), and solves it with the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) on a statevector simulator, cross-validated by an exact classical solver. Six industry profiles — banking, healthcare, IoT/edge, government, e-commerce, and defense supply criteria weightings grounded in sector requirements. The framework is delivered as a three-tier platform combining a React front end, a Spring Boot service layer with JWT-based role-controlled access, and a Python/Qiskit quantum microservice over PostgreSQL. To our knowledge this is the first framework to operationalize selection across the complete finalized NIST portfolio, converting sector requirements into an auditable, reproducible recommendation. Across all six profiles the QAOA solution recovers the exact optimum (approximation ratio = 1.0), validating the pipeline; we are explicit that at the four-algorithm scale this certifies correctness rather than quantum advantage, and the QUBO–QAOA formulation is carried as a forward-compatible path to NP-hard enterprise-portfolio selection. The contribution is a novel, deployable decision methodology and its engineered realization.

Across all six profiles the QAOA solution recovers the exact optimum (approximation ratio = 1.0), validating the pipeline; we are explicit that at the four-algorithm scale this certifies correctness rather than quantum advantage, and the QUBO–QAOA formulation is carried as a forward-compatible path to NP-hard enterprise-portfolio selection. The contribution is a novel, deployable decision methodology and its engineered realization.

title: AgentGuard-ZT: AgentDojo Workspace Benchmark Evaluation Dataset
abstract: This dataset supports the research manuscript "AgentGuard-ZT: Zero-Trust Runtime Authorization for Tool-Using AI Agents." It contains 210 valid AgentDojo workspace benchmark evaluations across three configurations: Undefended, Tool Filter, and AgentGuard-ZT v2.1, with 70 evaluations per configuration. The dataset documents legitimate-task utility, native prompt-injection objective success, and experimental configuration information. It enables comparative analysis of security–utility trade-offs in runtime authorization for AI agents. The benchmark results demonstrate zero native injection-objective successes for both Tool Filter and AgentGuard-ZT within the evaluated cases. However, AgentGuard-ZT achieved lower legitimate-task utility than Tool Filter. These results are specific to the evaluated benchmark and do not establish universal protection against prompt injection. The public dataset package excludes raw execution traces and potentially sensitive tool payloads.

title: Predicting unplanned readmissions in neurological patients: A large-scale AI-driven analysis using CHAID decision trees
abstract: BACKGROUND: Unplanned readmissions in neurology signify care gaps, increasing costs, and morbidity. This study aimed to develop and internally validate an AI model to predict unplanned readmissions among neurological patients in Jordan. METHOD AND MATERIALS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of 2,795 adult neurology admissions (2022-2024). Patients' diagnosis was grouped and analyzed based on the International Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision. Nine prediction models were compared using Electronic Health Record (EHR) data. The Chi-square Automatic Interaction Detection (CHAID) decision tree was selected for optimal performance and interpretability. RESULTS: The unplanned readmission rate was 8.9%, highest in the neoplasm group (24%). The CHAID model demonstrated modest discriminative ability (AUC = 0.671). For risk stratification, it achieved a balanced accuracy of 0.63, sensitivity of 0.52, and specificity of 0.74. Key predictors were Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI ≥ 5), age, geographic region, length of stay, and sex. Risk-stratification metrics were calculated descriptively from the complete cohort, whereas independent model validation was based on the held-out test-set AUC. Subgroup analysis revealed distinct risk profiles: vascular patients with high CCI (p < .001, χ2 = 66.368), young females of whom 37.3% had neoplasms (p = .037, χ2 = 4.367), and functional disorder patients from northern regions (p = .009, χ2 = 8.897). CONCLUSION: This is one of the first studies from the Middle East to demonstrate the potential of the CHAID model for risk stratification in neurology readmissions. The model offers an interpretable framework to identify high-risk patient subgroups but requires external validation before clinical application. Its poor-to-fair discriminative performance (AUC = 0.671) supports population-level risk stratification rather than individual-level prediction.

title: Architecting the quantum internet: from links to networks
abstract: Large-scale quantum networks will need communication protocols that make efficient use of limited physical resources while operating under loss, noise, and finite memory lifetimes. We present a unified approach to long-distance quantum communication that combines bosonic and continuous-variable error-correcting codes with quantum multiplexing and multipath resource aggregation. Using repeater-assisted architectures, we examine how encoded quantum information can be distributed across network paths of unequal length in a way that improves secret key rates, logical error performance, and end-to-end fidelity under realistic conditions. Our results show that quantum error correction must be treated as a network-level problem and provide practical design guidance for scalable quantum repeater networks beyond simple point-to-point links.

title: De Re and De Dicto Trust
abstract: Abstract De re/de dicto distinction is a well-known concept that differentiates between properties of non-rigid designators and the properties of the objects that they refer to. The article proposes to apply this distinction to the notion of trust. The technical results are formal definitions of de re and de dicto forms of trust as modalities, the proof of the undefinability of these two modalities through each other, and a sound and complete logical system capturing the properties of the two forms of trust.

title: Quantum Query Complexity of Maximum Degree and its Generalizations
abstract: We study the quantum query complexity of several basic graph problems. 1) We prove a tight $Θ(n^{3/2})$ bound for finding a maximum-out-degree vertex in an $n$-vertex tournament, resolving a conjecture of Mande, Paraashar, and Saurabh [FSTTCS'23]. 2) Using the same proof idea, we give a direct proof that finding a maximum-degree vertex in an $n$-vertex undirected graph requires $Θ(n^{3/2})$ quantum queries, a bound implicit in the work of Apers and Lee [CCC'21]. Both lower bounds above hold even for computing only the maximum degree or maximum out-degree. 3) We also study Maximum $(k,n-k)$-Cut, which asks for the largest cut with one side of size $k$. For every constant $k\geq 1$, we give an $O(n^{2-1/(k+1)})$-query quantum algorithm. 4) We establish a reduction to Maximum $(k,n-k)$-Cut involving $k$-Graph Collision, which asks whether the marked vertices of a known graph contain a $k$-clique. For $k\geq 3$, this yields unconditional lower bounds with exponents strictly larger than $3/2$, showing that this problem is strictly harder than computing maximum degree. Additionally, under a conjecture we propose for $k$-Graph Collision, the reduction yields a lower bound matching our upper bound above.

title: Gaussian BROJA Partial Information Decomposition in Closed Form
abstract: The BROJA partial information decomposition provides an operationally motivated way to separate the information that two sources carry about a target into unique, redundant, and synergistic components. For continuous and high-dimensional variables, however, computing the BROJA decomposition requires solving a difficult optimization problem. Previous work showed that, when each source-target pair is jointly Gaussian, the problem can be reduced to finite-dimensional numerical optimization. Here, we derive a closed-form solution to this optimization problem, enabling direct computation of the BROJA decomposition in the general multivariate Gaussian setting. The resulting closed-form expression enables speedups exceeding two orders of magnitude for high-dimensional Gaussian BROJA PID. Code is available at https://github.com/brainsandmachines/Eigen_PID.

title: Multi-Modal Graph Neural Network-Inspired Vessel Identification and Tracking for UAV-Based Maritime Surveillance
abstract: The unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based maritime surveillance is becoming an important part of maritime Internet of Things (IoT) and intelligent transportation systems. It provides a flexible and cost-effective way to large-scale maritime traffic monitoring. However, achieving robust situational awareness remains challenging in practical maritime environments. The main challenges arise from heterogeneous sensing modalities, adverse imaging conditions, and spatial misalignment caused by UAV motion. To address these problems, this paper proposes an airborne multi-modal graph learning-driven framework, termed AMGT, for vessel identification and tracking in UAV-assisted maritime IoT. Specifically, visible and infrared images are first aligned and fused through a multi-parameter perspective transformation model. This improves visual perception under low visibility and complex illumination conditions. Automatic identification system (AIS) messages are then temporally synchronized using interpolation and linear prediction. To detect small and oriented vessels, we develop a mixed-modality MAir-YOLOv8-OBB detector, followed by the MAir-SORT algorithm for stable vessel tracking. We further design a graph learning-driven association network to model temporal dynamics and spatial dependencies among vessels and between vessels and UAVs. A motion-aware coordinate unification (MCU) strategy is also introduced to reduce nonlinear misalignment caused by UAV motion. Experiments on the MAP-M2UAV50 dataset show that AMGT achieves high accuracy and efficiency. The results demonstrate its potential for UAV-assisted maritime IoT applications, including vessel monitoring, traffic situational awareness, and intelligent maritime transportation services. The dataset and code will be available at https://github.com/MAPGroup/AMGT.

title: OCaml's module language is the perfect fit for agentic programming
abstract: I've been doing a fair bit of agentic OxCaml programming in the past year, and consistently finding that OCaml is a perfect fit across the spectrum of languages I've been developing in recently. If you're not familiar with OCaml, this post is a quick guide as to why I think this. As codebases get larger, a coding agent is better at filling in a 'well-specified hole' than cramming in a million-line codebase into its context window.

title: Reproducibility code and data for A Square-Root Barrier to Quantum Gate Speed under Linear Coupling
abstract: This archive contains the production code, curated numerical data, and figure-generation scripts for the Gaussian waveguide calculations supporting “A Square-Root Barrier to Quantum Gate Speed under Linear Coupling” (arXiv:2609.19280, https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19280). It includes the first-moment Gaussian reference calculation; full qubit-field matrix-product-state simulations using a unitary Lanczos star-to-chain transformation and two-site time-dependent variational principle evolution; coherent and squeezed-state energy sweeps; endpoint convergence data; and scripts that recompute the reported least-squares coefficients, coefficients of determination, and sampled assumption bounds.

title: "O'ZBEK VA TURK TILLARIDA AVTOMATIK MORFOLOGIK TAHLIL VA LEMMATIZATSIYA: MASHINA TARJIMASI UCHUN ZAMONAVIY YONDASHUVLAR"
abstract: This article analyzes contemporary approaches to automatic morphological analysis and lemmatization in the Uzbek and Turkish languages, which have an agglutinative structure. It also highlights major linguistic challenges characteristic of these languages, including the large number of word forms (vocabulary explosion), homography, and phonetic changes, as well as their impact on Natural Language Processing (NLP) systems. The study comparatively examines the advantages and disadvantages of rule-based, statistical, and neural network-based approaches. In addition, existing morphological resources and corpora for both languages are analyzed, and recommendations are proposed for the use of highly effective hybrid models in practice and for the development of open morphological test datasets for the Uzbek language.

abstract: Статья посвящена исследованию технологии построения вполне интерпретируемых регрессионных моделей. Выдвинута гипотеза, что на первом этапе при реализации этой технологии в качестве экспертов в исследуемой предметной области могут привлекаться большие языковые модели. title: The role of artificial intelligence in the modern Russian economy innovative development
abstract: Innovation is now not just one of the possible paths of development, but the main condition for the survival of any enterprise. The key factor that changes the paradigm of the innovation process is the ability to delegate routine operations. Previously, a significant portion of highly qualified employees’ time was spent on data collection and preliminary information processing, which considerably slowed down the research and development cycle. Modern technologies make it possible to completely delegate trivial tasks to intelligent systems, which are capable of processing such information much faster than a human. In today’s environment, the integration of autonomous intelligent systems is crucial for reducing operational costs. In 2026, artificial intelligence has transformed from an auxiliary technology into an indispensable tool for ensuring the competitiveness of knowledge intensive enterprises. The main areas of application of artificial intelligence have been analyzed, including the automation of business processes, generative design, and predictive analytics of production equipment. The main barriers that limit the implementation of automation systems based on artificial intelligence have been systematized and identified. It has been established that artificial intelligence has changed the methodology of research and development work, reducing the product development cycle from several months to several weeks. The conclusion is formulated that the integration of artificial intelligence tools into production processes reduces costs, the percentage of defective products, and requires staff to develop creative and strategic competencies. The role of artificial intelligence is defined not merely as an automation tool, but as an active participant in the innovation process, capable of creating innovative solutions. An author’s classification of barriers to the implementation of artificial intelligence in knowledge intensive industries has been developed.

title: Final-cap study on the final views of a registered study of evidence delivery in an LLM agent network: preregistration
abstract: Preregistration of an add-on study to osf.io/pz3hg. Every final view of the source study's primary module (3,072 views; one system, google/gemma-4-31B-it) is asked again, fresh, under final output caps of 1,024 and 3,072 tokens, with all other request fields equal to those of the stored final call. The study estimates how the accuracy of fresh final answers on fixed final views differs between the two caps, and whether accuracy is higher under relay assist than under native routing with the larger cap. The source study's results were known when this study was planned; at registration no model call of this study had been made.

title: Below-threshold execution of fault-tolerant ripple-carry addition on a trapped-ion quantum computer
abstract: We deploy a universal fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) architecture based on error-detecting $[\![8,3,2]\!]$ and $[\![4,2,2]\!]$ codes on Quantinuum's Helios-1 trapped-ion quantum computer. We compile and execute ripple-carry adder (RCA) circuits for classical inputs up to five bits on this architecture. Uncomputing a workspace qubit provides an additional ``algorithmic check'' to detect errors. While available at both the physical and logical levels, this check synergizes with our architecture by increasing the effective fault distance of many circuit locations from two to four. Combining this algorithmic check with the error-detecting codes, we observed only a single logical failure in one-bit addition after burst-error filtering, yielding an estimated logical failure rate of $(6.0 \pm 5.9) \times 10^{-5}$. This is well below the $(3.5 \pm 1.3) \times 10^{-3}$ failure probability observed for one-bit addition on the same hardware in unencoded form. Two- and three-bit adders also showed performance improvements, while the longer four- and five-bit adders executed just above threshold.

title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?
abstract: Language models increasingly support or automate information retrieval from document collections too large to index. This task is difficult when it requires specialist linguistic or scientific knowledge. We used the Wikipedia Game to test language models on an analogous information retrieval task. In the game, players must reach a target article using only article links. We compared sentence embedding models and LLMs across five Wikipedia languages and five academic-literature datasets. We construct very large local graphs of Wikipedia pages and of paper citations using OpenAlex and provide code to build and navigate them. This allows the study of language models' navigation capabilities without relying on third-party APIs. We compared the models with human and TF-IDF benchmarks. The Wikipedia Game format enables robust comparisons across techniques, languages, and domains. No model significantly outperformed humans, although the best models (GPT-o3 mini, GPT-4o, QwQ:32B, and DeepSeek-R1:70B) achieved comparable success. Performance and rankings varied across languages and topics, with implications for practitioners utilising these techniques.

evidence.title: Can Language Models Play the Wikipedia Game?
evidence.abstract: Language models increasingly support or automate information retrieval from document collections too large to index. This task is difficult when it requires specialist linguistic or scientific knowledge. We used the Wikipedia Game to test language models on an analogous information retrieval task. In the game, players must reach a target article using only article links. We compared sentence embedding models and LLMs across five Wikipedia languages and five academic-literature datasets. We construct very large local graphs of Wikipedia pages and of paper citations using OpenAlex and provide code to build and navigate them. This allows the study of language models' navigation capabilities without relying on third-party APIs. We compared the models with human and TF-IDF benchmarks. The Wikipedia Game format enables robust comparisons across techniques, languages, and domains. No model significantly outperformed humans, although the best models (GPT-o3 mini, GPT-4o, QwQ:32B, and DeepSeek-R1:70B) achieved comparable success. Performance and rankings varied across languages and topics, with implications for practitioners utilising these techniques.

title: Adaptive DHiSparse: Speculative Decoding over a Load-Adaptive KV Hierarchy
abstract: Long-context serving runs out of KV memory before the hardware reaches its useful throughput. HiSparse stores history in host memory and fetches only the selected entries, but it uses one cache budget at every load and does not handle draft-model speculative decoding such as DSpark and DFlash2. We present Adaptive DHiSparse, which supports speculative decoding over hierarchical sparse KV and adapts residency to load. It protects the required working set, retains additional history while GPU memory is spare, and recovers the rest through exact fused retrieval. DSpark and DFlash2 keep their proposal and acceptance rules: queries share missing-row retrieval, draft KV uses a window-bounded ring, and verification staging is reused across layer groups. At 100K context and concurrency 128, GLM-5.3 with DFlash2 delivers 793 output tokens/s per decode GPU, 1.45$\times$ HiSparse and 1.27$\times$ non-speculative adaptive serving. Held to the same latency bounds as HiSparse, it sustains up to 4$\times$ the concurrency and 2.3 to 3.7$\times$ the output, depending on the per-token bound. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at 500K context and concurrency 512, Adaptive DHiSparse with DSpark delivers 1.85$\times$ the output of resident serving with DSpark. In a load step, optional residency reduces host fetches from 14.2% to 1.4% of selected rows at low load and releases memory under pressure.

title: Complexity-Calibrated Reconstruction Discrepancy for No-Reference Point Cloud Quality Assessment
abstract: The discrepancy induced by surface reconstruction in a distorted point cloud is jointly influenced by its intrinsic structural complexity and signal degradation. This observation motivates a referencefree point cloud quality assessment (PCQA) strategy that estimates and compensates for the complexity-induced component. We implement this strategy through successive reconstruction. Specifically, reconstructing the distorted point cloud produces an input-toreconstruction discrepancy that combines the effects of signal degradation and content complexity. Reapplying the reconstruction operator with stronger smoothing produces a discrepancy between successive reconstructions, which serves as a proxy for the complexityinduced component. This proxy is then used to calibrate the inputto-reconstruction discrepancy. We apply the same strategy to 3D geometry patches and their aligned 2D regions, enabling local comparison of the resulting discrepancies. The calibrated geometric and projected-view discrepancies are then fused into a final degradation score. For both branches, the discrepancies are measured using frozen pretrained perceptual representations. Our method does not require PCQA-specific training or fine-tuning. Experiments on three public databases show that the proposed method consistently outperforms most generic baselines and achieves performance comparable to several full-reference metrics.The code is available at https://github.com/HC-W-whc/CCRD-NR-PCQA.git.
