title: Sobolev-Regularized Filtering on Weighted Riemannian State Spaces for Kinematic Signal Recovery at Very Low Signal-to-Noise Ratio
abstract: Recovering a kinematically coherent signal from observations whose signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) lies far below 0 dB is a central difficulty in radar tracking under electronic countermeasures. Classical linear filters treat the observation as an unstructured scalar sequence and, at very low SNR, either discard the signal or require model assumptions that an adversary can violate. This paper develops a variational framework in which the observation is represented as a scalar field on a five-dimensional weighted Riemannian state space (planar position, planar velocity, acceleration magnitude) and is estimated by minimizing a variable-exponent Sobolev energy that couples a second-order smoothness penalty with a spatially adaptive data-fidelity term. We (i) establish existence and uniqueness of the minimizer, (ii) derive the optimality condition, including a curvature correction missing from the flat-space form, (iii) give a spectral bias-variance analysis showing that the estimator behaves as an adaptive low-pass filter whose achievable noise reduction is governed by the ratio of the observation dimension to the effective signal dimension, and (iv) obtain a mean-square error rate that matches the classical minimax exponent for Sobolev classes. Interactive Benchmark & Live Demo: https://5dvr.ai

title: OQIMLI SHIFRLARNING STATISTIK XUSUSIYATLARINI KOMPLEKS BAHOLASH: MARGINAL, JUFT VA SHARTLI MEZONLARNING QIYOSIY TAHLILI
abstract: Oqimli shifrlarni baholashda chiqish bitlari muvozanati, lavina xossasi va shartli bog'lanishlar turli xavfsizlik jihatlarini ifodalaydi. Ularni yagona xavfsizlik tasdig'i sifatida talqin qilish asossiz umumlashtirishdir. Ushbu ishda statistik qamrov, xatolik ehtimoli va amaliy og'ish chegarasini hisobga oluvchi metodologiya taklif etiladi. Unda maksimal marginal og'ish, juft XOR hamda ochiq IV guruhlari bo'yicha shartli tahlil qo'llaniladi. ChaCha va Trivium ustidagi tajribalarda Trivium432 uchun maksimal og'ish 0,132172 ga yetdi. N=131072, η=0,30 parametrida to'liq shartli usul siyrak nazoratni 27/32 holatda aniqladi, biroq uch bitli paritet nuqsonini aniqlamadi. Natijalar statistik dalil beradi, ammo real qurilma xavfsizligini isbotlamaydi.

title: Hybrid Adaptive Post-Quantum Cryptographic Framework (HybridMedPQC) with Optimized SPHINCS+ for Long-Term Medical Image Security
abstract: Quantum-capable adversaries threaten the long-term integrity of medical images exchanged through PACS/DICOM workflows, while post-quantum signatures introduce storage and latency trade-offs.This paper proposes HybridMedPQC, a tier-adaptive hybrid signing framework that combines CNN-and DICOM-assisted Image Sensitivity Classification with a policy-driven Adaptive Algorithm Selection Engine.For each image, Layered Signature Generation produces an inner archival anchor (SPHINCS+ or Dilithium/Falcon) and an outer transport signature (Dilithium or Falcon) bound with an RFC3161 timestamp to enable outer-first fast verification.A Long-Term Re-signing Protocol maintains archival validity by chaining refreshed signatures to prior records.Projected evaluation on 1024×1024 images shows up to 91.9% signature overhead reduction for the Standard tier and 81.2% for the Sensitive tier, versus standalone SPHINCS+, while preserving Falcon-level verification (~6-8 ms) and perfect image fidelity (SSIM=1.0,MSE=0, PSNR=∞).Critical-tier images retain NIST Level 5 defense-in-depth via SPHINCS+ plus Dilithium.

title: Human gradient artificial intelligence for self-aware learning systems
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) generally defines intelligence as an optimal association between input features and predictive behavior. In essence, it is defined as knowledge updating under adaptation, describing the static relationship between input features and decision accuracy in a human-interpretable form. This definition is not suitable for the cutting-edge colony of AI frameworks where intelligence evolves from fast, detailed, and organized learner AI agents. This paper introduces an innovative Human Gradient Artificial Intelligence (HGAI) approach to model intelligence as a measurable continuous gradient of knowledge updating under evolution with human-inspired behaviors such as metacognition-driven self-assessment, self-regulation, and self-reflection. In HGAI, pretrained machine learning models define AI agents to understand their evolutionary behavior by modeling gradient of knowledge updating with softmax probability, cross-entropy, stochastic gradient descent and regularization, while considering predictive performance over two phases of discrete time-steps. AI agents are also pretrained in the principal component basis of the original feature space. Additionally, confidence evolution over gradient is defined as an aggregated effect of high probabilities of predictions and the prediction losses to reflect metacognition-driven self-assessment. Trustability of knowledge update is also defined with the rolling statistics of losses and prior updated knowledge to integrate self-regulation and self-reflection. Experimental results of kernel-SVM, ridge-regression, Lasso, and Perceptron models, integrating fast, detailed, and organized learner AI agents with Digits and Fashion-MNIST datasets, show prediction accuracy in the second phases are generally higher (92-99%) for the fast and detailed learners. However, it is lower for the organized learners, satisfying higher accuracy in the second phase than in the first. The acceptance rate of gradient knowledge update is also high in all cases (85-100%). Additionally, confidence evolves steadily for all three types of learners of all the models, as models update their gradient knowledge. Hence, HGAI reflects gradient-based, self-aware evolutionary intelligence.

title: Interconnections in Clinical Treatment Measures at the Pan-Disease Level: A Deep Neural Network Analysis of SEER-Medicare
abstract: In outcomes research, clinical treatment measures are routinely analyzed. Most existing studies focus on individual diseases, and increasing recent evidence suggests that clinical treatment measures of different diseases can be “correlated” (or interconnected). Existing studies on such interconnections are usually limited to a small number of diseases. In this study, for U.S. older patients with common cancers, we complement the existing literature and conduct a pan-disease analysis of interconnections in clinical treatment measures. This effort can assist in better managing and planning healthcare resources. We mine SEER-Medicare for subjects diagnosed between January 2004 and December 2017 with esophageal, colorectal, liver, pancreatic, oral cavity/pharyngeal, lung, breast, prostate, renal/kidney, and bladder cancers. In the inpatient/outpatient treatment settings, a total of 113/168 diseases are analyzed. To accommodate unique data characteristics and our analysis goals, we develop a deep neural network (DNN)-based estimation approach, which adopts an additive two-part loss function to accommodate zero inflation, uses DNNs to capture nonlinearity, and applies penalization to identify interconnections. Extensive statistical and numerical investigations are conducted. In the data analysis, sensible findings are made for individual cancers, and across-cancer and across-setting analyses are also conducted. Supplementary materials for this article are available online, including a standardized description of the materials available for reproducing the work.

title: Local Diagnostics of Learned Event Representations for Anomaly Detection at the HL-LHC
abstract: Anomaly detection, the identification of collision events that deviate from Standard Model expectations, is one of the most promising model-agnostic strategies for new-physics searches at the Large Hadron Collider. Searching for rare events in learned low-dimensional representations removes the need to commit to hand-crafted observables a priori, but sacrifices the immediate physical interpretation those observables provide. For anomaly detection to enter a discovery pipeline, flagged events must therefore be diagnosed locally, both to distinguish potential new physics from mismodeling or detector effects and to identify observables for targeted follow-up searches. We evaluate supervised and self-supervised neural embedding strategies on COLLIDE-2V, a 750-million-event dataset simulated under realistic High-Luminosity LHC conditions, using the reconstruction error of an autoencoder trained in the learned latent space as the anomaly score. Across the configurations and benchmark signals considered, supervised objectives, which exploit simulation process labels during training, generally outperform their self-supervised counterparts and, in their best configurations, improve on an autoencoder trained directly on kinematic features, raising the signal efficiency at 10% background acceptance on all held-out processes. We further introduce a local diagnostic pipeline that fits a Gaussian Mixture Model to the SM latent space, profiles each component through high-level observables without process labels, localizes the flagged events, and ranks observables by their local discriminating power. The ranking recovers the defining kinematics of the held-out processes, while correlating the anomaly score with the same observables quantifies how closely the score tracks them, revealing cases where the most discriminating observable is not the one the score follows most closely.

title: MotionCoach: Constructing Multimodal Guidance for Video Professional Motion Editing
abstract: Video editing models achieve strong performance in modifying appearance, backgrounds, styles, and motions, empowered by large-scale training data. Beyond general scenarios, professional motions are significant in performance, sports, and martial arts. This paper focuses on professional motion editing, which involves fine-grained motion technique and temporal structure. Given professional motion names but lacking detailed descriptions, existing models often fail to generate professional motions, such as incorrectly lifting the front wheel under a Stoppie instruction. To address this challenge, we introduce MotionCoach, a trained multimodal agent that uses multi-turn tools and performs self-verification, producing a grounded prompt and a reference clip as reliable and sufficient multimodal guidance to inject external professional motion knowledge into video editing models. To supply training data, we build a data pipeline to construct trajectories. We cold-start the agent on MotionCoach-SFT-10k and apply Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) on MotionCoach-RL-2k with rewards on the motion guidance prompt, the motion outcome video, and the format. For evaluation, we introduce VPMEBench, comprising 314 professional motion editing tasks with fine-grained references and annotations. Extensive experiments show that MotionCoach improves the overall score from 55.1 to 65.6 on Seedance 2.0 and from 51.2 to 64.5 on MiniMax-H3. Learning to construct multimodal guidance enables precise professional motion editing without retraining video editing models.

evidence.title: MotionCoach: Constructing Multimodal Guidance for Video Professional Motion Editing
evidence.abstract: Video editing models achieve strong performance in modifying appearance, backgrounds, styles, and motions, empowered by large-scale training data. Beyond general scenarios, professional motions are significant in performance, sports, and martial arts. This paper focuses on professional motion editing, which involves fine-grained motion technique and temporal structure. Given professional motion names but lacking detailed descriptions, existing models often fail to generate professional motions, such as incorrectly lifting the front wheel under a Stoppie instruction. To address this challenge, we introduce MotionCoach, a trained multimodal agent that uses multi-turn tools and performs self-verification, producing a grounded prompt and a reference clip as reliable and sufficient multimodal guidance to inject external professional motion knowledge into video editing models. To supply training data, we build a data pipeline to construct trajectories. We cold-start the agent on MotionCoach-SFT-10k and apply Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) on MotionCoach-RL-2k with rewards on the motion guidance prompt, the motion outcome video, and the format. For evaluation, we introduce VPMEBench, comprising 314 professional motion editing tasks with fine-grained references and annotations. Extensive experiments show that MotionCoach improves the overall score from 55.1 to 65.6 on Seedance 2.0 and from 51.2 to 64.5 on MiniMax-H3. Learning to construct multimodal guidance enables precise professional motion editing without retraining video editing models.

title: SecFD-FL: Frequency-Decoupled Federated Learning with Secure Aggregation for Charging Load Forecasting in Internet of Electric Vehicles
abstract: Accurate charging load forecasting is essential for the reliability and efficiency of the Internet of Electric Vehicles (IoEV), yet it is challenging on two fronts: charging demand is highly stochastic, and the data collected by distributed sensors is privacy-sensitive. Although federated learning (FL) preserves data privacy, collaborative training still remains vulnerable to an honest-but-curious server that can invert shared model updates to reconstruct private data. To address both data volatility and privacy concerns, we propose SecFD-FL, a frequency-decoupled federated learning framework for IoEV comprising: 1) a dual-stream gated recurrent unit (GRU) network that separately models short-term and long-term charging load volatility, and 2) a lightweight secure aggregation layer for privacy preservation. Specifically, the secure aggregation layer employs a zero-sum additive masking protocol that perturbs each client's upload with high-variance noise, preventing the server from reconstructing private data while preserving the exact aggregate. Extensive experiments have been conducted on both EV-level and charging station-level using real datasets. The experiment results show that SecFD-FL reduces global RMSE by up to 60% over centralized baselines, achieving Jain's fairness up to 0.991 across clients, and reduces DLG-attack reconstruction correlation by 8 times to 15 times relative to FedAvg -- all with no additional per-round communication cost beyond a one-time key exchange.

title: Semantic Data Governance and Collaborative Architecture for LLM-Based Natural Language Analytics in Urban Rail Transit
abstract: Urban rail transit data are distributed across heterogeneous operational systems, where inconsistent semantics and fragmented metric definitions complicate the controlled use of large language models (LLMs) for natural language analytics. This study proposes a semantic data governance and collaborative analytics architecture for this setting. A lakehouse-based data foundation, a semantic middle layer, and a unified metric store are used to organize physical schemas, business terminology, and statistical definitions. Domain rules, network topology, and a controlled execution workflow are then introduced to constrain query generation and support cross-domain analysis. Two representative scenarios—power-supply fault assistance and passenger-flow–traction-energy analysis—are used to illustrate how data governance, knowledge augmentation, and execution validation work together. The contribution is an engineering architecture and its semantic governance mechanisms rather than a comparative evaluation of general-purpose LLM algorithms. The proposed approach provides a practical reference for integrating LLM-based analytics with existing urban rail transit data environments.

title: Measuring Model-Side Longitudinal Effects Under Scripted User Pressure: Multi-Turn Sycophancy as a Controlled Test Case
abstract: This publication presents a staged experimental methodology for investigating how repeated user pressure, corrective interventions, conversational history, and intervention withdrawal influence subsequent large language model behavior. Its central concern is the inadequacy of isolated-turn evaluation for characterizing effects that may persist, decay, accumulate, reverse, or redistribute across different behavioral dimensions over the course of an interaction. Multi-turn sycophancy is selected as the initial controlled test domain because it permits externally adjudicable tasks, systematic manipulation of user-expressed positions, and measurable distinctions between appropriate correction, unsupported agreement, factual calibration, and resistance to invalid pressure. The proposed methodology uses scripted, non-reactive users to isolate model-side responses without introducing uncontrolled reciprocal changes in human participants. The experimental program consists of four conditional stages. Stage 0 establishes measurement validity, including human-annotated calibration, inter-rater reliability, automated-judge validation, noise estimation, script-coherence assessment, and simulation-based power analysis. Stage 1 screens corrective mechanisms through randomized comparisons of adjudicated counterevidence, independent-first judgment procedures, and explicit anti-accommodation instructions against matched placebo conditions. Advancement requires predefined effect-size thresholds, multiplicity-controlled statistical evidence, and protection against deterioration in the other co-primary outcome. Stage 2 investigates intervention scheduling, examining correction dose, inter-delivery spacing, and terminal-recency schedule contrasts for mechanisms demonstrating sufficiently reliable effects during screening. The design explicitly identifies the algebraic dependence between terminal recency and intervention onset under a fixed withdrawal boundary, preventing unsupported causal attribution to either variable independently. Stage 3 examines conversational-history dependence and transport, testing whether different prior reinforcement histories alter subsequent correction responses and whether observed relationships replicate across held-out tasks, topics, or materially different model configurations. The framework employs paired user-position perturbations, evidence-controlled tasks, schedule-matched placebo conditions, a fixed correction-free withdrawal horizon, and subsequent valid-versus-invalid correction probes. Its co-primary outcomes are post-withdrawal calibrated accuracy and counterfactual stance sensitivity. Secondary measurements include correction selectivity, explicit agreement, framing acceptance, counterevidence coverage, linguistic accommodation, cross-dimensional displacement, and restricted mean maintenance duration. Particular attention is given to distinguishing genuine corrective improvement from superficial behavioral compliance. A reduction in explicit agreement does not necessarily indicate improved calibration if unsupported framing becomes more influential, counterevidence receives less consideration, or valid subsequent corrections are rejected. Similarly, an immediate corrective response does not establish that the effect persists once the intervention is withdrawn. The methodology integrates established techniques from sequential experimental design, intervention research, longitudinal robustness evaluation, survival analysis, mixed-effects modeling, and multiple-comparison control. Its contribution lies in their bounded assembly into a model-side measurement program with explicit progression criteria, falsification conditions, replication requirements, and stopping rules. The work is informed by existing research on sycophancy, conversational-history effects, persona drift, epistemic drift, resonant amplification, and human consequences of AI accommodation. These research programs are treated according to their respective evidentiary and methodological relevance, without assuming that their mechanisms are interchangeable or that broader reciprocal phenomena can be established through scripted-user experiments. An earlier related preprint by the author provides a limited conceptual distinction between behavioral mechanisms and observed trajectory classes. The present methodology does not require those proposed trajectory classes to occur and does not assign them explanatory authority in advance of experimental observation. This publication is a methodological proposal, not a report of completed experimental findings. It makes no empirical claim that the proposed correction mechanisms produce durable benefits, that longitudinal effects necessarily accumulate, or that the experiment demonstrates reciprocal human–AI epistemic drift. Human belief revision, trust formation, relational escalation, and other reciprocal adaptations remain outside the direct scope of the initial experiment and require subsequent human-participant research. The intended contribution is a reproducible framework for determining which longitudinal model-side relationships are observable, statistically distinguishable, durable, transferable, and potentially predictive. Positive, negative, and null findings are equally informative within the specified experimental boundaries. The broader objective is to replace assumptions about conversational accumulation or corrective persistence with explicit measurements of temporal response, intervention dependence, and cross-dimensional behavioral change. Publication status: Proposed experimental methodology; empirical validation pending. Keywords: model-side longitudinal evaluation, multi-turn sycophancy, scripted user pressure, correction selectivity, conversational history, intervention scheduling, withdrawal, durability, calibration, cross-dimensional displacement.

title: Indonesian Social Assistance Regulations Dataset for AI-Based Public Service Chatbots
abstract: This dataset contains Indonesian government regulatory documents related to social assistance programs. It was compiled to support research and development of AI-based public service chatbots, particularly retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems that answer questions about social assistance regulations. The dataset serves as a regulatory knowledge source for a research project investigating a Regulation-Aware Multi-Query Retrieval Framework. The framework is designed to support the processing of user queries containing multiple information needs by retrieving relevant regulatory evidence for each query or intent. Dataset Contents The dataset consists of regulatory materials related to social assistance programs. The exact document types, issuing authorities, publication dates, and source URLs should be documented in the accompanying metadata or README file, where available. Intended Use The dataset is intended for research on: AI-based public service chatbots; Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG); Regulatory information retrieval; Multi-query and multi-intent query processing; Evidence-grounded response generation and evaluation. Data Provenance and Processing The accompanying documentation should identify the original sources of the regulatory documents and describe any extraction, cleaning, text normalization, chunking, or other processing applied to the data. Any processed representation should be distinguished from the original source documents. Limitations The dataset represents the regulatory materials included in this release and should not be assumed to cover all Indonesian social assistance regulations or all regulatory updates. Users should verify the current validity and applicability of individual regulations against their official sources before relying on them for legal or administrative decisions. Citation and Reuse Please cite this dataset using its Zenodo DOI after publication. Reuse and redistribution are subject to the license specified in the record and any applicable rights or conditions associated with the original source documents.

title: The Ghost v0.02: From Declared Erasure to Measured Disappearance Crypto-shredding, scrypt audit, time window, and GSM8K evidence
abstract: Il presente lavoro valuta un meccanismo di ragionamento intermedio con cancellazione verificabile, denominato Fantasma. La versione 0.02 aveva introdotto tre livelli di garanzia (L1,L2, L3) e un’indagine pilota su 50 problemi GSM8K. La versione 0.03 estende la valutazione inquattro direzioni: (i) un braccio di controllo reformulate-then-answer privo di cifratura, al fine didistinguere l’effetto del doppio passaggio computazionale dall’effetto del sigillo crittografico; (ii)un’analisi sistematica dei casi di errore secondo una rubric predefinita; (iii) una rassegna dellaletteratura pertinente, con riferimenti verificati; (iv) una misura quantitativa del trafilamentoinformativo tra pensiero interno e riformulazione. I risultati su 50 problemi (seed 20261010)indicano: Direct 47/50, Hidden-CoT 45/50, Fantasma 47/50, ReformOnly 46/50. Il meccanismodi sigillo non incrementa l’accuratezza rispetto al controllo. Il codice numerico non comparemai nella riformulazione (0/50); la similarit`a ROUGE-L della riformulazione rispetto al pensierointerno `e pari a 0.308, rispetto alla domanda originaria a 0.733. Si documenta un error-modeproprio dell’architettura a due chiamate. Non si avanzano affermazioni di significativit`a statisticaoltre il perimetro del pilota. This work evaluates an intermediate-reasoning mechanism with verifiable erasure, termed theGhost. Version 0.02 introduced three guarantee levels (L1, L2, L3) and a 50-problem GSM8Kpilot. Version 0.03 extends the evaluation in four directions: (i) a reformulate-then-answercontrol arm without encryption, distinguishing the effect of two-pass computation from the effectof cryptographic sealing; (ii) systematic failure analysis under a predefined rubric; (iii) a reviewof the pertinent literature with verified references; (iv) quantitative measurement of informationleakage between internal thought and reformulation. Results on 50 problems (seed 20261010) are:Direct 47/50, Hidden-CoT 45/50, Ghost 47/50, ReformOnly 46/50. The sealing mechanism doesnot increase accuracy over the control. The numeric code never appears in the reformulation(0/50); mean ROUGE-L of the reformulation against internal thought is 0.308, against theoriginal question 0.733. A two-call error mode is documented. No statistical significance isclaimed beyond the pilot scope.

title: Понимание как удержание концепта и проверка языковых моделей (к методологии исследования)
abstract: Аннотация. В статье ставится вопрос: правомерен ли вывод о понимании языковыми моделями той или иной предметной области на основании выполнения ими сложных тестовых заданий. Обосновывается неправомерность такого вывода и указывается логическая ошибка: в умозаключении не распределён средний термин. Незамеченной ошибка остаётся по причине, к логике прямого отношения не имеющей, но зафиксированной при анализе формата изложения: в разборе С.С. Аверинцевым византийской риторики он показывает, что каноническая форма изложения сообщает выводу достоверность прежде, чем проверено содержание. Высокий процент в таблице результатов проверки языковых моделей и является такой современной формой, на что обращают внимание профессионалы при оценке качества языковых моделей. Логическая несостоятельность указывает на содержательную — тестовые наборы проверяют знание, тестируя верность суждений, в то время как заключение делается о понимании, единицей которого является не суждение, а связь. Чтобы возразить по существу, договариваться о природе понимания не требуется: достаточно указать наблюдаемое следствие, которое из приписывания понимания обязано вытекать. Такое следствие есть. Концепт как смысловое целое, стоящее за словом, дан в нескольких формах — в понятии, образе и действии; целое присутствует в каждой из них, и потому понимание связано со способностью переходить между формами данности, узнавая в другой то же самое и удерживая единство смысла. Если переход не осуществляется и наблюдается разрыв, это однозначно свидетельствует об отсутствии понимания, хотя бы владение отдельными формами присутствовало. Установлен режим работы критерия: провал перехода опровергает приписывание понимания, успех его не удостоверяет, — и для задач оценки первого достаточно. В работе использованы методы: логический и категориальный анализ, операционализация конструкта, историко-культурная аналогия и модельный случай, внешняя валидация через смежные дисциплины. Abstract. The article poses the question of whether it is legitimate to infer that language models understand a given subject domain from the fact that they solve difficult test items. Such an inference is shown to be illegitimate, and the error is named: the middle term of the syllogism is undistributed. The error goes unnoticed for a reason that has nothing to do with logic: in S.S. Averintsev's analysis of Byzantine rhetoric, the author shows that a canonical form of exposition confers credibility upon a conclusion before its content has been verified. A high percentage in a table of language-model evaluation results is precisely such a contemporary form. The logical failure points to a substantive one: benchmarks test knowledge by assessing the correctness of judgements, whereas the conclusion is drawn about understanding, whose unit is not the judgement but the connection. To object on the merits, no agreement about the nature of understanding is required: it suffices to specify an observable consequence that must follow from the attribution of understanding. Such a consequence exists. A concept, the semantic whole standing behind a word, is given in several forms — in the notion, the image and the action; the whole is present in each of them, and understanding is therefore expressed in the ability to move between the forms, recognising in one the same thing as in another. If the transition does not take place and a break is observed, this unambiguously testifies to the absence of understanding, even where command of the separate forms is present. The operating mode of the criterion is established: failure of a transition refutes the attribution of understanding, while success does not certify it — and for the purposes of evaluation the former is sufficient. The methods used are: logical and categorial analysis, operationalisation of the construct, historico-cultural analogy and the model case, external validation through adjacent disciplines.

Установлен режим работы критерия: провал перехода опровергает приписывание понимания, успех его не удостоверяет, — и для задач оценки первого достаточно. В работе использованы методы: логический и категориальный анализ, операционализация конструкта, историко-культурная аналогия и модельный случай, внешняя валидация через смежные дисциплины. Abstract. The article poses the question of whether it is legitimate to infer that language models understand a given subject domain from the fact that they solve difficult test items. Such an inference is shown to be illegitimate, and the error is named: the middle term of the syllogism is undistributed. The error goes unnoticed for a reason that has nothing to do with logic: in S.S. Averintsev's analysis of Byzantine rhetoric, the author shows that a canonical form of exposition confers credibility upon a conclusion before its content has been verified. A high percentage in a table of language-model evaluation results is precisely such a contemporary form. The logical failure points to a substantive one: benchmarks test knowledge by assessing the correctness of judgements, whereas the conclusion is drawn about understanding, whose unit is not the judgement but the connection. To object on the merits, no agreement about the nature of understanding is required: it suffices to specify an observable consequence that must follow from the attribution of understanding. Such a consequence exists. A concept, the semantic whole standing behind a word, is given in several forms — in the notion, the image and the action; the whole is present in each of them, and understanding is therefore expressed in the ability to move between the forms, recognising in one the same thing as in another. If the transition does not take place and a break is observed, this unambiguously testifies to the absence of understanding, even where command of the separate forms is present. The operating mode of the criterion is established: failure of a transition refutes the attribution of understanding, while success does not certify it — and for the purposes of evaluation the former is sufficient. The methods used are: logical and categorial analysis, operationalisation of the construct, historico-cultural analogy and the model case, external validation through adjacent disciplines.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Deep Learning Approach for Lung Tumor Identification
abstract: Lung cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths worldwide, affecting millions of people every year. Early and accurate detection is significant for providing suitable treatment and improving patient survival. Computed Tomography (CT) scan images are widely utilized in lung cancer diagnosis because they provide detailed information about lung tissues and abnormalities. Recently, quantum computing has also been explored in medical image analysis owing to its potential to process complex and high-dimensional data more efficiently. Therefore, this study introduces a Quantum Computing-based Framework for Enhanced Lung Cancer Detection (QCF-ELCD) using CT images. The proposed QCF-ELCD framework involves advanced pre-processing steps to enhance the image quality and uniformity within the data. The hybrid feature extraction process integrates ConvNext architecture along with an efficient channel attention mechanism. This combination extracts highly discriminative features, which are then forwarded to the quantum fidelity-based classification algorithm. The classifier enhances the model's performance by identifying the class with the maximum quantum fidelity match. Moreover, the AdaBelief optimizer is employed to improve model parameters during training, contributing to improved classification performance. Additionally, Grad-CAM++ is utilized to visualize the discriminative regions learned by the proposed QCF-ELCD, thereby improving model interpretability and clinical transparency. The experimental analysis of the QCF-ELCD framework is conducted using the IQ-OTH/NCCD Lung Cancer Dataset and LIDC-IDRI Dataset, achieving promising classification accuracy of 95.13% and 94.23%, respectively. Consequently, the proposed QCF-ELCD framework demonstrates its potential as an effective tool for automatic lung cancer classification, outperforming existing models.

title: Secure Over-the-Air (OTA) Firmware Update Mechanism for Resource-Constrained Embedded Devices
abstract: Software embedded design systems are also penetrating more and more important areas of application: the Internet of Things (IoT), remote health monitoring, industrial automation, and smart infrastructure, current safe efficient and secure firmware update mechanisms are paramount. The ability associated with over-the-air (OTA) updating of firmware is strictly required in preserving the functioning of devices, exploiting such gaps, and empowering the features after release. But in highly constrained systems (those with limited memory, processing capacity and available energy), conventional secure update interfaces can incur unacceptable overheads or they may not provide complete protection against sophisticated cyber-attacks. In this paper the authors introduce a simple yet lightweight and robust OTA update mechanism built specifically to be used on such constrained platforms. This suggested framework combines the familiar AES-GCM-authenticated encryption to guarantee data confidentiality and integrity, a source authentication technique based on checking digital signatures secured using ECDSA, and a versioning protocol providing the anti-rollback protection using monotonic counters. As part of validating its practicality, the solution is applied and tested with ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers, i.e., STM32 and nRF52840, where communication is performed over low-power wireless networks like LoRaWAN and BLE. A signature of firmware packages via custom-built update server (TLS) will provide secure transfer of updated packages. Experimental scrutinisms indicate that the secure OTA system has very limited overhead in resources (about 14 KB extra flash usage and 3 KB of RAM) and the average update speed is 3.8 seconds with a 256 KB binary image using LoRaWAN. In addition, the system is well adapted to identify and discard a tainted or old firmware image, hence ensuring device immunity against attacks including firmware manipulation, replay, and man-in-the-middle intrusion. The performance highly conforms to the contention that the framework provides a robust degree of security and performance coupled with resource usability hence being ideal to use in real fully embedded applications that have strict limitations. This contribution consists of a scalable, secure OTA approach that builds resilience to the operational integrity and trustworthiness of the distributed embedded system in dynamic and security critical settings.

title: Can machines reason non-verbally?
abstract: Modern machines can solve equations, follow logic and reason through language, yet they still struggle with problems that require visual non-verbal reasoning. This is evident even in advanced systems such as DeepSeek, ChatGPT and Gemini, which remain limited on visual tasks such as completing abstract patterns or delineating ambiguous regions-of-interest. Unlike explicit intermediate steps in verbal reasoning which can be verified through logic or automated tests, visual reasoning involves implicit intermediate steps with no clear methods for verification. Non-verbal reasoning is therefore challenging to model and, as a result, remains a fundamental limitation of current machine intelligence. Here we introduce GenVerOpt, a general framework that unifies generation, verification and optimisation into a reasoning pipeline for machines. By generating candidate solutions, verifying their correctness, and iteratively refining them, GenVerOpt enables per-sample optimisation rather than relying solely on dataset-level trends captured during model training. This process mirrors human problem-solving where multiple possibilities are imagined, evaluated, and refined until a correct solution emerges. Across diverse domains, GenVerOpt demonstrates capabilities beyond existing systems: it surpasses humans on abstract IQ puzzles, matches clinicians in prostate cancer segmentation, exceeds experts in liver vessel reconstruction and outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in tumour boundary alignment. These results show that machine reasoning can extend beyond language, establishing visual non-verbal reasoning as a foundation for more flexible and generalisable intelligence.

title: X-AVDD: Cross-Attentive Audio-Visual Dataset Distillation
abstract: Audio-visual dataset distillation aims to synthesize a small dataset from a large paired audio-visual dataset, while nearly preserving the training utility for neural networks. Existing approaches such as DM and AVDD face two critical limitations: 1) they are memory-intensive, making them difficult to scale to complex architectures and higher samples-per-class (SPC) settings, and 2) they often fail to preserve strong cross-modal semantic correspondence. To tackle these issues, we propose X-AVDD, a cross-attention-based distillation method that explicitly captures inter-modal relationships during synthesis. By decoupling cross-modal alignment from joint optimization, X-AVDD is substantially more memory-efficient, reducing end-to-end synthesis cost by $\sim 8\times$ GPU-hours, while producing highly aligned synthetic data. Empirically, X-AVDD significantly outperforms other audio-visual distillation methods. On VGGSound, an audio-visual dataset of short YouTube clips, X-AVDD improves top-1 test accuracy from $8.2\%\rightarrow24.0\%$ at SPC=$10$ and $9.8\%\rightarrow26.5\%$ at SPC=$20$. Furthermore, X-AVDD improves cross-architecture generalization (e.g., $25.5\%\rightarrow35.3\%$ for a ViT target on AVE dataset at SPC $=50$) and successfully scales to complex architectures such as AudioCLIP, achieving $62.3\%$ accuracy using only $5.65\%$ of the full dataset, against the full dataset accuracy of $72.4\%$ while completing in $9\times$ lower training time compared to the full dataset.

title: Entanglement Catalysis Beyond the Asymptotic Rate
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental resource in quantum information science, commonly consumed to perform tasks like quantum teleportation and quantum key distribution. Entanglement concentration converts partially entangled pure states into nearly perfect Bell pairs. While its efficiency is well understood in the asymptotic limit, practical protocols must operate with finite systems. In this finite regime, and at the low error levels relevant in practice, performance is penalized by corrections that reduce the achievable yield. We investigate whether this fundamental finite-size penalty can be mitigated by an entanglement catalyst: an auxiliary state that aids the transformation but is returned exactly and uncorrupted. Although such a catalyst cannot increase the leading-order asymptotic yield, we show that it fundamentally alters the finite-size scaling. For every bipartite pure state with nonuniform Schmidt coefficients, we exactly determine the optimal second-order correction to the yield and show that catalysis completely overcomes this finite-size penalty.

title: PPG-Bench: A Unified Benchmark for PPG Foundation Models
abstract: Photoplethysmography (PPG) is increasingly recorded by wearable and clinical devices at enormous scale, and a growing number of PPG foundation models (FMs) have been developed to compute reusable representations for various downstream tasks. These models are difficult to compare: different evaluations use different datasets, task definitions, preprocessing, downstream heads, hyperparameter tuning, and baselines. We present PPG-Bench, a unifying open-source benchmark evaluating five public PPG FMs across nine open-access datasets and 26 tasks spanning cardiovascular state estimation, activity, sleep, screening, and identification. We evaluate models under four downstream regimes of increasing adaptability (linear probing, random forests, frozen MLP probes, and end-to-end finetuning), with model-specific hyperparameter optimization and subject-disjoint cross-validation. We also evaluate against three controls: random/constant baseline, a deterministic pulse-rate-variability (PRV) feature set, and a generic time-series FM (MOMENT). Across all 68 task-regime combinations, 35.3% show no meaningful FM advantage over the random/constant baseline, and in 83.8% no PPG-specific FM outperforms both PRV and MOMENT. We also find that added downstream head capacity generally improves performance, but can cause significant degradation if the model is performing at chance/constant level. Current PPG FMs therefore cannot yet claim to provide generalised and transferrable representations of PPG signals, and future evaluation in this field should include checks against simple, non-learned controls. Code for the benchmark and instructions to evaluate more models can be found here - https://github.com/mannas-ai/ppg-bench.

title: MVGraph: Benchmarking LVLMs on Evidence Composition across Multi-View Visual Graph
abstract: We introduce MVGraph, a benchmark for evaluating large vision-language models (LVLMs) on multi-graph reasoning where the evidence required by a query is distributed across multiple interrelated visual graph views. Although such evidence commonly resides in source-specific graphs, temporal snapshots, or local observations, existing graph reasoning benchmarks remain confined to a single self-contained structure, assessing only graph perception and reasoning while leaving the alignment and composition of evidence across views underexplored. MVGraph comprises 8k instances spanning 8 \textit{graph-theoretic} tasks, abstracted from two multi-graph scenarios (partial and temporal graph views). Each problem is programmatically constructed and verified to be unsolvable from a single view. Beyond end-to-end evaluation, we decompose multi-graph reasoning into four complementary capabilities---Perception, Alignment, Composition, and Reasoning---and design 29 diagnostic tasks with 64k instances to probe each one, along with golden intermediate representations for evaluating the intermediate process. Across 15 LVLMs, we reveal the difficulty of multi-graph reasoning and identify cross-view edge alignment and relation-level composition as prominent bottlenecks through stage-oriented diagnostics. Meanwhile, temporal constraints and increasing view counts expose further capability boundaries. Code and data are available at https://github.com/AAAndy-Zhu/MVGraph.

title: Extending ElectionGuard with Eligibility Verifiability to Prove the Absence of Ballot Stuffing
abstract: ElectionGuard is a cryptographic toolkit that makes elections end-to-end verifiable but leaves eligibility verifiability open. Without this property, ballot stuffing, i.e., the addition of ballots beyond one per eligible voter, cannot be detected from the election record. This thesis extends ElectionGuard with eligibility verifiability while preserving its applic­ ability to different voting systems and the simplicity of its verification. Every ballot is signed under a credential whose key shares are generated independently by several regis­ trars using a multi-signature scheme, so that the registrars can only collectively produce a usable credential. In addition, the electoral roll is fixed by a perfectly hiding commitment, which allows designated auditors to inspect the same roll the credentials were issued for without publishing it. It is proven that, as long as one registrar is honest, the extension is verifiable under the unforgeability of the multi-signature scheme and the soundness of the tally proofs. The correctness of the roll itself is established by a statistical audit whose error probability is bounded by the number of sampled entries. Since the published credentials carry no reference to a voter, everlasting ballot privacy is preserved as long as the registrars keep the link between voters and credentials secret. A prototype of ElectionGuard instantiates the construction with MuSig and a Pedersen commitment. Election records produced by it remain valid for unmodified verifiers, and the benchmarks show a constant overhead of about one kilobyte and less than one millisecond per ballot, which amounts to about 4% for the smallest ballot style evaluated and decreases for larger ones.

title: Breaking the Quantum Memory Wall on Consumer Silicon: Exact 28-to-53 Qubit Sub-Manifold Contraction and Paraconsistent Thermodynamics on a Single 4GB GPU
abstract: The classical emulation of quantum supremacy circuits and large-scale industrial quantum optimization is fundamentally bottlenecked by the exponential Hilbert-space "Memory Wall" (O(2^N)). Standard simulation frameworks (such as IBM Qiskit Aer and NVIDIA cuQuantum) suffer immediate Out-of-Memory (OOM) crashes on commercial GPUs (4GB VRAM) when attempting universal state-vector simulation at N = 28 qubits, while brute-force supercomputing approaches—exemplified by the 41.9-million-core New Sunway system—require 1.3 Petabytes of RAM and 15 Megawatts of power to resolve the 53-qubit Google Sycamore circuit (m = 20) in 304.4 seconds. In this work, we present the unified Chronos-Quantum Engine, a proprietary GPU microarchitecture operating within a strict 3.58 GB VRAM ceiling on a single 60W laptop GPU (NVIDIA RTX 3050 Ti). We demonstrate three verified operational regimes on physical silicon: (1) Exact 28-Qubit Universal State-Vector Evolution (268,435,456 complex states confined to 2.147 GB VRAM) achieving IEEE-754 exactness (L2 error = 8.32 × 10^-12 against FP64) for real-time industrial QAOA optimization and long-time Floquet-MBL discrete time-crystal dynamics; (2) Full 53-Qubit Sycamore Circuit Resolution (S = 128 coherent phase partitions across all 20 layers and all 1,555 gates with zero omissions), achieving global unitarity ||Ψ||^2_2 = 0.99998384, unbiased Porter-Thomas second moment ⟨u2⟩/⟨u⟩2 = 2.014852 (0.038% relative error from theoretical ideal), and Linear Cross-Entropy Benchmarking fidelity FXEB = 1.014852 (1.039321 under Born quantile sampling) in 372.34 seconds—consuming 204,383× less energy and 338,540× less memory than Sunway; and (3) Supremacy Threshold Crossing in 2.96 seconds (Slice 1, FXEB = 0.0235 > 0.002) alongside 783 ms Paraconsistent L4 Thermodynamic Screening at the 95% Overlap Gap Property (OGP) barrier.

title: KL Before and After Mixing: A Round-Complexity Separation in Parallel Sampling
abstract: A parallel sampler can choose at random which coordinates to generate together. For a target $p$ and the output law $q_U$ of a schedule $U$ drawn afresh for each output, we compare the schedule-averaged divergence $\mathbb{E}_U D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q_U)$ with the output-law divergence $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|\mathbb{E}_U q_U)$, in nats. Rounds commit independent draws from exact conditional marginals frozen at the round's start, each output's schedule is drawn before sampling from a finite mixture of schedules, and every scheduled round is charged. title: CNN-Transformer with Sigmoid Label for High-Resolution Sub-Degree DOA Estimation
abstract: This paper addresses the grid quantization error of deep-learning (DL)-based direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation. Classification- based DOA methods discretize the continuous angular space into a grid, so that with a peak-based read-out, the accuracy and resolution are limited by the grid step and by the width of the label peak. To address this issue, we propose a sigmoid label that encodes the sources' DOAs as the sum of angle-shifted monotonic sigmoid functions. Differentiating the output of a CNN-Transformer network trained with the sigmoid label produces sharp spectral peaks at the source DOAs. Combined with a moderately refined grid step of 0.25 degrees, the CNN-Transformer with the proposed sigmoid label attains sub-degree accuracy and a 1-degree resolution, breaking the limit of the grid quantization error. Under the unified CNN-Transformer backbone, we compare the proposed Sigmoid label with the Gaussian label, the 0-1 hard label, and the binary cross-entropy (BCE) baseline. Numerical results demonstrate that the Sigmoid label attains the highest accuracy and superior resolution compared to other labels.

title: DataCupid: Stable Matching Repair for Training Data Acquisition with Delayed Feedback
abstract: Matching repair after utility changes can reuse valid observations, but new evaluations must respect matching capacity and may return out of order. We study announced invalidations with bounded, possibly reward-dependent reporting delays and pending evaluations that do not occupy future matching capacity. Residualload repair (RLR) combines sound outcome certificates with batched matching schedules for unequal sample deficits. Its complete dyadic quota schedule admits a sharp issue-round bound with coefficient cb < 1.607 relative to the terminal residual endpoint load, together with separate delay and evidence-lifetime bounds. RLR-P monitors complete issue-order prefixes without changing the sampling plan before acceptance. With a deterministic pure oracle, a single-repair coupling from the same drained initial state guarantees no increase in certification time, issued observations, or time to a reusable checkpoint. We also derive an information-load lower bound. On fixed priority-star markets with unknown Bernoulli gaps, PrioritySearch attains the history-adjusted first-order constant for expected certification time as δ {\sim} 0, under hypothesis-independent linear history scaling and sublogarithmic reporting delays. Paired simulations and measured-feedback replay quantify the trade-offs: in the replay, RLR-P has lower mean capped update-certification time than a monitored width-based baseline, at higher oracle CPU cost.

title: Vulnerable Models in the AI Supply Chain: An Empirical Study of Adoption, Propagation, and Usage Patterns
abstract: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) models has established a complex supply chain, but many of these shared artifacts harbor severe vulnerabilities such as insecure serialization and architectural backdoors. While prior efforts have extensively scanned model registries to flag malicious artifacts, a critical gap remains in understanding how developers actually adopt and integrate these unsafe models into downstream software systems. We bridge this gap by conducting a large-scale empirical study on the usage and propagation of 16,977 known vulnerable models on HuggingFace flagged by InsightDB. We track their prevalence across GitHub repositories, software packages, fine-tuning chains, and deployed applications. Our analysis reveals that, despite being publicly flagged, these vulnerable models appear in over 21,000 code locations across more than 5,000 open-source repositories, with 3,757 distinct flagged models (22.1\%) actively referenced in at least one project. To understand how these models are integrated in code and identify recurring usage patterns, we categorize and analyze the recurring patterns surrounding them via a customized pipeline that combines Code Property Graphs extraction with a tailored Frequent Subgraph Mining approach. Across all patterns, we find no evidence of provenance verification or model sanitization logic, with developers frequently bypassing security parameters or delegating trust to permissive framework defaults. These findings underscore that scanning model files alone is insufficient, highlighting the urgent need for context-aware security analysis and stricter integration guardrails at the application layer of the AI supply chain.

title: Dictionary-Based Attention for Hyperedge Reweighting
abstract: We introduce Dictionary-based Attention (DA), a label-free, support-preserving block that reweights existing vertex–hyperedge memberships using dictionary-code similarity. We evaluate local dictionaries with closed-form hypergraph learning (DA-HL) on visual data and a separate shared-dictionary variant with a static incidence network on citation data. Supplementary experiments under an explicitly reconstructed visual protocol cover nine dataset–generator combinations. Four DA-versus-uniform comparisons reach the 0.05 threshold after Holm correction; the three clustering settings show no mean advantage under the original stopping rule with an iteration cap of 200. In paired clustering runs extended to 5000 iterations, mean accuracy is practically stable between 4000 and 5000 iterations within a prespecified one-percentage-point margin, but weights, propagation operators, and some predictions continue to change. This does not establish convergence or equivalence to the original 12-iteration budget. In transductive citation experiments, test features participate in shared-dictionary fitting; the paired static-backbone results are negative on Cora, close to zero on Citeseer, and slightly positive on Pubmed, with only Pubmed meeting the multiplicity-corrected threshold. Additional controls separate injected-membership ranking from downstream classification and show sensitivity to weight mapping and member-specific assignment without identifying a unique gain mechanism. The evidence supports benefits in some tested visual configurations, rather than broad effectiveness across hypergraph learning.

title: Structured phenotypes from unstructured reports: large language model extraction of chest CT identifies mortality subgroups in emergency department dyspnea
abstract: Acute dyspnea is among the most heterogeneous emergency department (ED) presentations, and no validated framework exists for postdiagnostic risk stratification across its underlying causes. Chest CT reports describe the intrathoracic organs well beyond the presenting complaint, yet this information is rarely reused. We aimed to derive and externally validate mortality phenotypes in ED dyspnea by combining routine laboratory data with large language model (LLM) extraction of chest CT reports. In a multicenter retrospective cohort of 51,843 adults (2016–2025) with acute dyspnea undergoing chest CT at three Korean teaching hospitals, claude-sonnet-4-6 extracted 18 imaging findings per report using a prespecified JSON schema. Phenotypes were derived in one hospital ( n = 12,702) by k-means clustering of 12 routine clinical and laboratory variables plus graded imaging features, then applied unchanged to two external validation hospitals ( n = 17,395; n = 21,746) by frozen-centroid nearest-cluster mapping. We also compared graded (0–3) features with binary features derived from the same extraction by thresholding at severity ≥ 1, holding every downstream step identical. Three phenotypes reproduced across all three hospitals: Well (37.9–40.6%), Inflammatory-Parenchymal (21.1–25.3%), and Cardiac-Vascular-Congestive (34.1–40.5%). Compared with Well, adjusted hazard ratios were 2.43–3.90 for Inflammatory-Parenchymal and 2.81–3.44 for Cardiac-Vascular-Congestive (all P < .001); unadjusted ratios were 2.77–5.11 and 3.27–4.70. Phenotype membership was largely unchanged when age was removed from the feature space (adjusted Rand index 0.80–0.82), and the phenotypes were recovered in pre-pandemic, peak-pandemic, and post-pandemic strata. Graded and binary features gave similar incremental discrimination: adding phenotype indicators to an age- and sex-adjusted Cox baseline raised Harrell C-index by 0.041–0.054 with graded and 0.040–0.053 with binary features (paired difference 0.0010–0.0022). Routine chest CT reports, converted to structured data by an LLM and combined with routine laboratory values, identify reproducible mortality phenotypes in ED dyspnea that carry age- and sex-independent prognostic information across hospitals with differing case-mix. Binary features derived from the same extraction performed similarly, so retaining ordinal severity added little in this pipeline.

title: AADL: a lightweight anti-aliased multi-scale network for CT pulmonary nodule detection
abstract: Accurate detection of pulmonary nodules in CT images is important for early lung cancer screening, but remains difficult because nodules vary widely in size, shape, and density. Tiny and low-contrast nodules are particularly challenging, as their weak margins and vessel- or pleura-like appearances often lead to missed detections or false positives. This study proposes AADL, a lightweight pulmonary nodule detector designed to preserve fine details during multi-scale feature extraction. HU normalization and 2.5D slice fusion are first used to incorporate limited inter-slice context into a two-dimensional framework. A CSP-DSFA module with SimAM attention is then introduced to enhance local texture representation and boundary responses for small nodules. To reduce the loss of fine structures during resolution reduction, an anti-aliased downsampling module smooths features before subsampling, replacing conventional strided convolution. A lightweight shared convolutional head is further used to reduce redundant parameters across prediction branches. On LUNA16 and LNDb, AADL achieves mAP@0.5 values of 95.8% and 65.2%, respectively, outperforming the YOLOv11n baseline by 3.7 and 4.4 percentage points while reducing the parameter count to 2.11M. In addition, zero-shot evaluation on the Ali Tianchi dataset shows more stable external performance, suggesting that AADL provides a compact detector with improved cross-domain robustness for CT pulmonary nodule detection.

title: Goal-Oriented Bundle Management and Flow Control for Deep-Space Communications via Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Deep-space communications operate under intermittent connectivity, long propagation delays, and relay storage constraints. In such networks, the Bundle Protocol enables store-carry-forward communication, requiring relay nodes to manage limited storage and scarce contact opportunities. Relay-side scheduling and dropping decisions are inherently goal-oriented: transmission resources should be allocated to bundles most valuable to downstream mission objectives. Conventional schedulers, such as FIFO, do not explicitly optimize task utility and may provide unfair service across heterogeneous planetary sources. This paper presents a closed-loop modeling and learning framework for relay-side bundle and flow management in a contact-driven deep-space network, where lunar and Martian updates are forwarded through a shared-buffer relay to Earth. We quantify destination-side information freshness using excess age $Δ_i^e(t)=[Δ_i(t)-d_i(t)]^+$, where $Δ_i(t)$ denotes the Age of Information of source $i$ and $d_i(t)$ is a source-dependent delay baseline. Based on this metric, we define a goal-oriented loss that supports source-dependent nonlinear penalties, allowing prioritization according to mission relevance. We formulate relay control as a constrained semi-Markov decision process (CSMDP) and solve it using masked Lagrangian Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). Feasibility-aware action masking restricts transmissions to bundles that can complete within the remaining contact window. DTNSim simulations indicate improved age-based utility and inter-flow fairness compared with baseline schedulers. The proposed framework jointly optimizes relay-side bundle scheduling, dropping, and flow control under contact-driven dynamics with explicit fairness considerations across heterogeneous sources.

title: Retractions Revisited: A Replication, Extension, and Mechanistic Evaluation of Linguistic Obfuscation Effects in Fraudulent Science
abstract: Prior work suggests fraudulent scientists write their articles with higher rates of linguistic obfuscation than genuine scientists, with a possible mechanism suggesting obfuscation makes research more costly for a reader to analyze. This result has not undergone additional empirical scrutiny in the open science era, nor have other psychological mechanisms been evaluated. The current replication and extension addressed this opportunity by comparing 800 fraudulent and 800 genuine control papers (2013-2025). The results supported the linguistic obfuscation hypothesis, suggesting fraudulent papers were more obfuscated than genuine ones. A parallel mediation model evaluated three competing mechanisms, finding that reality monitoring, as measured through decreased rates of adjectives, best explained the link between fraudulent science and linguistic obfuscation. Cross-validated detection accuracy using obfuscation features (60.7%) and an elastic net of over 100 language dimensions (71.6%) were significantly greater than chance. Implications for scientific fraud and psychology of language research are discussed.

title: Finite-Size Limits of Adaptive Pauli Prediction
abstract: Can quantum data reliably answer questions chosen from earlier results? We prove that $M$ adaptive Pauli predictions on $n$ qubits require $Ω(\sqrt{\min\{n,M\}})$ copies at fixed accuracy. Published upper bounds make this tight for $M\le n$. Thus $n$ adaptive predictions cost $Θ(\sqrt n)$ copies, whereas a fixed list costs only $O(\log n)$. The lower bound uses diagonal states and commuting observables, identifying a statistical cost of adaptation. We also quantify how this cost increases with precision.

title: Prediction-Informed Landing Window Planning for UAV Landing on USV in High Sea States
abstract: Autonomous landing of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) on unmanned surface vehicle (USV) is difficult in high sea states. Existing hierarchical landing methods often infer future USV motion only implicitly from short observation histories, which limits their ability to adapt to severe and rapidly changing sea conditions. This paper presents a prediction-informed hierarchical control framework. A pretrained model is developed to explicitly predict the USV attitude during high-level landing decisions. The prediction helps identify suitable landing windows and choose the right touchdown time, while a conventional low-level flight controller maintains UAV stability and tracks motion commands. To evaluate the framework under realistic disturbances, a real-sim validation setup is constructed in which USV-motion data collected in real sea conditions are transferred to a MuJoCo USV. The experiments demonstrate the feasibility of using explicit attitude prediction to improve landing-window selection and support timing-aware UAV landing planning in rapidly varying marine environments.

title: Video Codec-Guided Training-Free Token Compression for Video Large Language Models
abstract: Video large language models (VLLMs) rely on long visual token sequences to understand complex temporal content, which makes visual token compression important for efficient inference. Existing training-free compression methods mainly reduce the number of tokens sent to the language model, but the compression process itself can still require many visual feature comparisons, especially for intra-frame token protection and inter-frame temporal token merging. This paper proposes a video codec-guided training-free token compression method for VLLMs that uses coding information already available in compressed video as a low-cost search prior. The method aligns reference-frame dependencies, motion vectors, and residuals with the visual token grid. Residual information forms compact candidate pools for token protection, while motion information is propagated along reference-frame chains to construct localized candidates for temporal token merging between sparsely sampled frames. Local visual feature similarity comparison is then used within these candidates to make the final compression decisions, without modifying the base VLLM. Experiments on three representative VLLMs and four video-understanding benchmarks show that the proposed method achieves performance comparable to the state-of-the-art training-free baseline FlashVID, and in some settings surpasses it, while substantially reducing the feature comparisons required by token protection and temporal matching. These results demonstrate that codec information can effectively improve the accuracy-complexity tradeoff of video token compression.

title: Deterministic Spectral Quantum Emulation on Classical Hardware
abstract: DSM–861 is best understood as a deterministic spectral computing architecture built from a rigid finite graph, a toroidal Hodge geometry, nonlinear KAN transport, vorton-inspired skew coupling, and associative-memory snapping. The arithmetic anchor is 861 = 42,2= T41 = 3 · 7 · 41, while the interaction topology is exactly J(42, 2) with degree 80 and spectrum {80, 38, −2}. The toroidal layer supplies a genuine discrete differential calculus. The finite-state theorem fixes the exact nine-qubit boundary of a single 861-dimensional core. The controllability theorem converts universal computation into a concrete Lie-algebra calculation. The snapping theorem supplies a mathematically correct route to non-accumulating numerical error through a deliberately constructed quadratic attractor.The resulting program is therefore executable as mathematics and engineering. Build the graph. Build the Hodge operators. Construct the control generators. Compute their Lie closure. Implement the nonlinear snap. Measure the ϵ2 law. Synthesize the FPGA. Then benchmark complete circuits. If those tests succeed, DSM–861 becomes a demonstrated deterministic spectral processor rather than merely a conceptual analogy to quantum computing.

title: Amortization collapse for reference stabilized geometric Rényi superchannel divergences
abstract: Preprint, version 1 For every real order 1 < α ≤ 2, we prove that the reference-stabilized geometric Rényi divergence of two finite-dimensional deterministic physical superchannels equals its nested amortized extension. Joint inserted channels A R → B R and the external state references in the inner channel divergences range over all positive finite dimensions. The proof combines a supported matrix perspective transformer inequality with a comb contraction, a completion of positive testers, and a physical realization of positive definite testers. It includes singular supported operators and gives value +∞ for unsupported comb pairs. In the supported case, the ordinary supremum already has the same value at reference dimension |C||A||B|. A conventional proof is presented alongside a correspondence with a Lean 4 theorem and a reproducible source artifact. The result concerns the nested quantity of Hirche's Eq. (39); it does not establish collapse of the larger fully amortized quantity in Eq. (40). AI contribution and provenance. This work was developed through an AI-assisted research process initiated and directed by Vinícius Mohr. GPT-6.1-Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 agents carried out the mathematical exploration, Lean formalization, proof development, critical review, and literature searches. GPT-6.1-Sol wrote the manuscript, including the conventional proof exposition reconstructed from the formal sources. Vinícius Mohr initiated the research by directing the agents to investigate open problems from the Quantum Information and Quantum Computation Open Problem Zoo using a lean-orchestrator framework, and subsequently requested verification and manuscript preparation. A detailed account of the respective human and AI roles, proof provenance, and verification procedure is provided in the manuscript and accompanying repository.

title: A Reproducible Evaluation Framework for TF-IDF-Based Machine Learning in Sentiment Classification
authors: Mr. Bhusare Ganesh Pravin and Prof. J. R. Mahajan
abstract: Sentiment analysis is an important Natural Language Processing (NLP) task used to automatically identify the emotional orientation expressed in textual data. Although recent research increasingly focuses on deep learning and transformer-based language models, classical machine-learning methods combined with Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) remain useful because of their relatively low computational requirements and reproducibility. This paper presents a controlled evaluation framework for comparing classical machine-learning classifiers for binary sentiment classification using the Large Movie Review Dataset (IMDb). The dataset contains 50,000 labeled reviews divided into 25,000 training and 25,000 testing reviews. Logistic Regression, Multinomial Naive Bayes, and Linear Support Vector Machine are evaluated using a common preprocessing and TF-IDF pipeline. On the fixed 25,000-review test set, Linear SVM achieved the highest accuracy of 90.196% and F1-score of 90.153%, followed by Logistic Regression with 89.936% accuracy and 89.980% F1-score. Multinomial Naive Bayes achieved 87.280% accuracy and 86.933% F1-score. The results demonstrate that controlled classical-model baselines can provide strong performance while remaining computationally accessible and reproducible.

title: Sentiment Analysis of Indonesian Mobile Banking Reviews on Google Play Store in 2025: A Comparison of Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: Mobile banking applications generate large volumes of user reviews that can be used to evaluate digital banking service quality. This study analyzes sentiment in Indonesian mobile banking reviews on the Google Play Store in 2025 and compares the performance of Naive Bayes (NB), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Random Forest (RF). A total of 270,977 reviews were collected from five applications, namely BRImo, Livin’ by Mandiri, myBCA, BYOND by BSI, and wondr by BNI. The data were processed through text cleaning, case folding, tokenization, word normalization, stopword removal, and negation retention. Sentiment labels were generated automatically using the InSet Lexicon and validated on 450 stratified review samples. The validation results showed moderate agreement between automatic and manual labels, with an accuracy of 0.6111, macro-F1 score of 0.5384, and Cohen’s Kappa of 0.4167. Review texts were represented using TF-IDF with unigram and bigram features, and model performance was evaluated across six stratified data-splitting scenarios using accuracy, macro precision, macro recall, macro-F1, confusion matrix, and macro ROC-AUC. The results show that RF in Scenario 6 achieved the best performance, with an accuracy of 0.9524, macro-F1 score of 0.8498, and macro ROC-AUC of 0.9798. Dominant-term analysis indicates recurring complaints related to login failures, transaction errors, system disruptions, and application updates. This study contributes a cross-application comparison of machine learning algorithms for Indonesian mobile banking sentiment analysis and provides practical insights for improving service reliability. However, the findings should be interpreted within the limitation of automatic lexicon-based labeling, particularly for neutral and context-dependent reviews.

title: Sensing with several different qubits (15m)
abstract: Following my previous talk in the same session, focused more on explaining the fundamental science, I will focus in this talk on sensing applications. Specifically, I will introduce some recent work on advanced sensors emanating from the work described earlier, including clock interferometry [1], point-source interferometry [2], and levitated particles [3,4]. Finally, time permitting, I will also describe our Yb optical lattice clock. title: DyssomniaNN: Multi-Scale Spiking Neural Modeling of Human Sleep Disorders and Perceived Restedness
abstract: Clinical sleep medicine repeatedly documents profound divergences between objective sleep duration and subjective daytime impairment, notably exemplified by sleep state misperception in paradoxical insomnia and boundary instability in narcolepsy type 1. Here, we present DyssomniaNN: a multi-scale biophysical computational framework coupling Borbély's two-process regulation of sleep homeostasis and circadian drive with Saper's hypothalamic reciprocal flip-flop circuit and a recurrent corticothalamic leaky integrate-and-fire spiking neural network. We formalize five clinical cohorts across an identical 72-hour photoperiod: healthy control, circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder (delayed-phase), chronic insomnia, paradoxical insomnia, and narcolepsy type 1. The synthetic local field potential converges closely with empirical human electroencephalography spectra from the PhysioNet Sleep-EDF database across all canonical frequency bands (spectral mean absolute error of 0.33--0.35). Furthermore, we introduce the Well-Rested Index to quantify restorative efficacy. Simulations reveal that sleep duration fails to predict restorative recovery: paradoxical insomnia achieves normal total sleep time (21.15 h) yet yields low restoration (37.6%) from unsuppressed cortical beta-band intrusion, whereas hypocretin deficiency in narcolepsy produces severe nocturnal fragmentation (781 min of wake after sleep onset) and 35 sleep-onset rapid eye movement periods. DyssomniaNN provides an in silico platform for mechanistic sleep research and virtual neuropharmacology.

title: On the Encoding of Calendar Features in Covariate-Informed Time Series Foundation Models
abstract: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) increasingly offer covariate support, with calendar information being the most common type of categorical covariate in practice, as it is available for every point in time. However, how these features are encoded is largely treated as an implementation detail rather than as an object of study, despite encoding being one of the few design choices left for pretrained models at inference time. With the present study, we demonstrate that the way information is propagated into the model substantially affects forecast accuracy of TSFMs. Therefore, we systematically compare seven calendar encodings, including three conventional target-agnostic representations (ordinal, one-hot, and cyclic) and four target encodings, across four state-of-the-art TSFMs on nine datasets from multiple domains in a zero-shot rolling evaluation. The nine datasets are influenced by social activities, such as weekends and holidays, making calendar information particularly relevant for forecasting. We find that encoding choice affects forecast accuracy across all models, with MASE differences of up to 9.9 % on non-holidays and 83 % on holidays within a single model. Effectiveness and utilization vary substantially across models. Improvements are concentrated around holidays, where calendar information provides signals unavailable from target history, while some model encoding combinations also improve non-holiday forecasts. A SHAP-based attribution analysis locates the contribution of the covariates relative to the autoregressive component and explains why some model-encoding combinations degrade performance. Our findings suggest that current benchmarks for covariate-informed TSFMs can distort model comparisons by imposing fixed encoding strategies.

title: Destination-Conditioned Adaptation with Semantic-Geometric Alignment for Generative Inbetweening
abstract: Generative inbetweening aims to synthesize temporally coherent intermediate frames between a start frame and a target frame. Although pretrained image-to-video diffusion models provide strong priors for large-motion inbetweening, they are not explicitly designed to reach a specified target frame. They may therefore generate realistic individual frames while drifting from the target or producing unstable motion under large displacements and non-rigid dynamics. We propose DSG-GI, a framework that adapts pretrained latent video diffusion models through \textbf{D}estination-Conditioned Adaptation and \textbf{S}emantic-\textbf{G}eometric Alignment. Destination-Conditioned Adaptation treats the target frame as the destination of the sequence and provides temporally progressive guidance along the generated trajectory. Semantic-Geometric Alignment aligns the token-wise spatio-temporal relational geometry of backbone features with that of a frozen video foundation encoder and applies a flow-matching-aware latent flow constraint to samples near the data endpoint of the probability path. Together, these components strengthen destination guidance and preserve coherent semantic-geometric motion structure. Extensive experiments on standard and large-motion inbetweening benchmarks demonstrate improvements in temporal stability, target-frame faithfulness, and perceptual quality. Our code will be made publicly available.
